Tips for searching with Slack AI

Use these tips to get the best results possible when searching with Slack AI.

Searching in Slack using AI

** Start simple**

To get an answer from Slack AI, ask it a question like you’d ask a friend. Straightforward questions and those that start with “What” or “How” tend to work best:

  • “How do I request content translations?”

  • “What does EOD stand for?”

Slack AI has trouble with subjective questions (for example, “When will the Acme deal close?”) and will be more likely to return inaccurate results for open-ended queries about the future.

** Keep your source material in mind**

Slack AI draws from information you and your coworkers share in (you guessed it!) Slack, rather than the internet at large. Unless you work in ecology, you’re unlikely to have luck with questions like “Do platypuses lay eggs?”

Tip: Slack AI may also return results for searches that aren’t phrased as questions if it seems likely that a response would be helpful, ex. “Project Acme timeline” or “Engineering offsite dates.”

** Lean on citations**

Answers from Slack AI will often include citations with links to source messages for you to reference alongside the provided answers. Hover over the number in brackets to view a snippet of a message referenced in an AI answer, or click on it to view the original message.

Learn more: Visit Guide to Slack AI for an overview and FAQs.

Track your sales pipeline with Slack CRM

View and manage your sales pipeline in one place with the Sales Tracker view in Slack CRM. Sales Tracker gives you a clear picture of your entire pipeline, so you can move leads forward, log activity, and work with your team to close deals.

Note: Sales Tracker is available to new Slack CRM customers only. We appreciate your patience as we make it available to more customers.

How it works

  • When you set up Slack CRM, Sales Tracker will be automatically enabled and a Sales Tracker tab will be added to your sidebar.
  • Anyone with access to Slack CRM will be able to use Sales Tracker.
  • Any contact you add to Slack will appear in Sales Tracker as a new lead. Move customers through the stages of the sales pipeline and add relevant details to their records like deal amounts, account names, and more.

Sales pipeline stages

A sales pipeline is a visual representation of where potential customers are in the buying process. When you open the Sales Tracker, you’ll see your customers arranged in a sales pipeline split into stages. Here are the stages you’ll see by default:

  • New Any new customer you add.
  • Contacted You’ve reached out to a lead and are awaiting a response.
  • Qualify You’ve confirmed a customer as a legitimate lead. When you move a lead into the Qualify stage, they’re converted to an opportunity.
  • Propose You’ve sent a customer an offer or quote.
  • Negotiate Your customer has responded to your quote and you’re working out the details of the deal.
  • Closed Won You’ve signed the deal. 🎉

Note: Move a lead to Unqualified or an opportunity to Closed Lost to remove it from your sales pipeline.

Use Sales Tracker

  1. From your desktop, click Sales Tracker in your sidebar.
  2. To move customer records to different stages in the pipeline, drag and drop them.
  3. Open a customer record view and update it, then select Save Changes.

Tip: To log activity like a call or email, click Quick Actions from a record, then select New Event.

Email a lead

Email a lead right from Sales Tracker to keep all your communication in one place and findable in Slack.

  1. From Sales Tracker, click a lead to open it.
  2. Click Quick Actions, then select Send Email
  3. Compose your message, then click Send Email.

Note: Sending emails using Slack is designed for direct, one-to-one customer communication and can’t be used for commercial or marketing emails.

How leads become opportunities

When you move a customer from Contacted to Qualify, their record will be converted from a lead to an opportunity. You’ll be automatically prompted to add additional details to the customer contact to keep track of their information.

  1. From Sales Tracker, move a customer to the Qualified stage.
  2. Enter an Opportunity name and Deal amount.
  3. Review the new record details, then select Convert Lead.
Customize your view

Filter or sort Sales Tracker to surface what’s important to you, like your biggest opportunities or leads that haven’t been updated this week.

  1. From Sales Tracker, click Edit view.
  2. To filter your view, click Filter, then select a field type and follow the prompts.
  3. To adjust how the view is sorted, click Sort, then choose an option.

Who can use this feature?

  • Members with access to Slack CRM
  • Available on the new version of the Business+ plan

Triage notifications from the Activity tab (legacy)

Use the Activity tab on desktop or mobile to quickly review all of your notifications. Think of it as a place to focus your attention or to get caught up after some time away from Slack.

Image of the Slack desktop app, with a cursor pointed at the Activity icon.

Work from the Activity tab

Click or tap the Activity icon on desktop or mobile to open a chronological feed of your notifications. Select a filter to switch between the different types of notifications, like mentions, replies to threads, or reactions to your messages.

  • A dot or numbered badge on a message in the feed indicates unread activity.
  • Use the Unreads button to see only new activity, and use the tabs to filter between different types of notifications.
  • Select a message to reply to it, or click the three dots icon on desktop for additional options, like opening the message in Home to read it in channel, setting a reminder, or summarizing the thread.

Note: If you’ve configured your notifications for all new messages in a channel, only those that mention you will show in Activity.

Filter activity

Each notification type that appears in the Activity tab has its own filter. Using the filter tabs along the top of the notification feed, you can adjust the feed to see specific notifications, or switch to All to see all your latest notifications.

  • All – View all your notifications in chronological order.
  • Mentions – Messages you’ve been mentioned in will be listed with the name of the conversation, the name of the person who mentioned you, and a preview of the message.
  • Threads – A list of replies to threads you’re following, or threads you’ve been mentioned in.
  • Reactions – When someone reacts to any of your messages, the message and all its reactions will show up in the Activity tab.
  • Apps – View messages from apps, like Google Calendar invitations or updates from JIRA.
  • Invitations – View invitations to collaborate in Slack. This includes Slack Connect invitations, channels you’re added to, and canvases that have been shared with you.
  • VIP – All activity between you and people you’ve added to your VIP list. (Available on paid plans)

Tip: On desktop, keep the Activity tab open at all times by opening it in a separate window.

Activity badge notifications

By default, the Activity icon and Slack app icon (if enabled) will show a numbered badge for every unread notification. Reactions to your messages will never display a badge, and if you’d like, you can exclude replies to threads you’re following from applying to the numbered badge count.

Exclude thread replies from Activity badges
  1. From your desktop, click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Select Preferences from the menu to open your notification preferences.
  3. Under Sound & appearance, check or uncheck the box next to Include thread replies in badge count on Activity.

If you’ve configured your preferences to exclude thread replies from the badge count, notifications will display as follows:

  • A dot badge Indicates the only unread notifications in Activity are replies to threads.
  • A numbered badge Indicates you have unread mentions, invitations and app notifications.

Note: On mobile, the badge on the Activity icon will always be a dot, and a numbered badge will appear on the workspace icon with unread activity in the workspace switcher.

Who can use this feature?

  • All members and guests
  • Available on all plans

Troubleshoot huddles screen sharing bug on the Slack Mac desktop app

We’ve identified a bug with screen sharing on huddles that impacts Mac desktop users who switched from the direct download version of Slack to the Mac App Store version. If you’re seeing an error when trying to share your screen even though you granted Slack access to screen recording, read on for steps you can take to resolve this issue.

Issue overview

  • This bug may impact you if you’ve switched from the direct download version of Slack to the Mac App Store version.
  • When you try to share your screen on a huddle, you’ll see an error prompting you to allow screen recording access in your Mac system settings.
  • In your system settings, it will appear as if Slack has already been allowed access, and toggling the permission will have no effect. As a result, you won’t be able to share your screen.

Steps to troubleshoot

If you’re experiencing this issue, you have a few options to get back up and running.

Manually remove Slack from apps with access

Remove Slack from the list of applications that are allowed access to screen recording. When you do, you’ll be able to successfully allow access next time you share your screen on a huddle.

  1. Click the Apple icon in the top-left corner of your screen, then select System Settings.
  2. Select Privacy & Security in the sidebar on the left, then select Screen & System Audio Recording.
  3. From the list of applications, click Slack.
  4. Click the - minus icon in the bottom-left corner of the list of applications.
  5. Quit and reopen the Slack desktop app, and follow the prompts to allow screen recording access next time you share your screen.
Run a terminal command

Use a terminal command to remove Slack from the list of applications that are allowed access to screen recording. The next time you share your screen on a huddle, you can allow Slack access to screen recording.

  1. Open a Finder window, then select Applications.
  2. Search for and open the Terminal app.
  3. Enter the following command: tccutil reset ScreenCapture com.tinyspeck.slackmacgap
  4. Quit and reopen the Slack desktop app, and follow the prompts to allow screen recording access next time you share your screen.
Switch back to the direct download version

Switching back to the version of Slack you were previously using will resolve the permissions issue in your system settings. Once you switch back, you won’t be prompted to allow screen recording access.

  1. Uninstall the existing Slack desktop app from your computer.
  2. Visit slack.com/downloads/mac.
  3. Click Download.
  4. Once the download is complete, open a Finder window and select your Downloads folder.
  5. Open the Slack .dmg file. This will open a small window.
  6. Drag and drop the Slack icon to the Applications folder in the window.
  7. To re-open the Slack app, open the Applications folder and click the Slack icon, then sign in.

Still having trouble? Our Support team is here to help. If you have any questions, let us know.

Understand the Primary Owner role

The Primary Owner is the most powerful administrative role in Slack. You can become a Primary Owner by creating your own workspace, or if a Primary Owner chooses to transfer ownership of a workspace or Enterprise organization to you. Keep reading to learn more about this role, and how to make sure the right person is in it.

Understand Slack’s ownership policies

To understand the Primary Owner role, it’s helpful to get familiar with Slack’s ownership policies. The Primary Owner has ultimate decision-making capabilities, and represents the Customer in administering the workspace.

  • If you use your corporate email domain to create a workspace or organization, your organization is the Customer.
  • If your workspace is set up by someone not formally affiliated with an organization, the Customer is the person who created the workspace.

To learn more about how we define the Customer, please review our Terms of Service.

Choose the right Primary Owner

Free, Pro, and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

The Workspace Primary Owner holds the highest level of permissions in Slack — only this person can delete the workspace or transfer ownership to someone else. There can only be one person in this role at a time, so it’s important to make sure it’s the right one. Here are some recommendations:

  • An executive or senior-level manager
  • Someone from the IT department who provisions licenses or handles account administration
  • If within the policy guidelines of your organization, use a shared service/administrative email account on your company’s domain that is managed by authorized personnel

The Org Primary Owner holds the highest level of permissions in Slack — only this person can transfer ownership of the org to someone else. There can only be one person in this role at a time, so it’s important to make sure it’s the right person. Here are some recommendations:

  • An executive- or senior-level manager
  • Someone from the IT department who provisions licenses or handles account administration
  • If within the policy guidelines of your organization, use a shared service/administrative email account on your company’s domain that is managed by authorized personnel

Transfer primary ownership

Because organizations change over time, Slack makes it possible to transfer ownership of a workspace or Enterprise org to someone else. We recommend adding a step to your company’s off-boarding process to make sure a departing employee can transfer ownership before they leave.

If the Primary Owner leaves before transferring ownership, we may be able to help, but this is not something we can guarantee. We recommend using the best practices for Primary Owners below to help maintain your workspace.

Best practices for Primary Owners

As the Primary Owner of a workspace or Enterprise org, use the following tips to help you administer Slack.

Assign Owners, Admins, and billing contacts
  • Promote Owners and Admins to help with day-to-day administrative tasks, like managing invitations or channels. Or, assign members to system roles (only available on Enterprise plans).
  • Add billing contacts, like people from the accounting department, to keep them informed of billing activity.
Keep administrative accounts on the corporate domain
  • Make sure all of your Owners and Admins use their company email addresses to join your Slack workspace or Enterprise org.
  • If your company’s email domain changes, the Primary Owner — and any other affected member — should update their email address in Slack.

Security guidance for desktop app updates

Since version 4.14.0, Slack release notes will include security guidance to help customers prioritize updating the Slack desktop app, if applicable. Here’s how to interpret different levels of guidance:

  • Guidance statement – What it means
  • This release includes minor security improvements. Updating is beneficial. – Minor security improvements. Upgrading will provide users with limited security benefits.
  • This release includes security improvements. Updating is recommended. – Some security improvements. Upgrading will provide users with security benefits.
  • This release includes significant security improvements. Updating is strongly recommended. – Significant security improvements. Users will gain significant benefits from upgrading, and should prioritize updating to the new version.

Note: Security guidance shouldn’t be construed to mean that older versions of the Slack desktop app are insecure. We’re constantly working to reduce the likelihood and data security impact of security issues. We always directly inform customers of any compromise impacting the security of their Slack workspace or client applications.

Updates to feature availability and pricing for Slack plans

In June 2025, we announced a set of changes coming to Slack plans that expand access to AI, security, and Salesforce features. To support the inclusion of advanced AI features, we changed the price of our Business+ plan and also introduced a new Enterprise+ plan.

Note: For details on plans and pricing, visit the Slack pricing page or contact our Sales team.

What to expect

  • Customers on the Free and Pro plans now have access to additional security features and basic Salesforce integration features.
  • Two AI features, conversation and thread summaries and huddle notes, are available to all customers on paid plans.
  • The Slack AI add-on is no longer available to purchase on the Slack website. Customers who purchased the add-on will continue to pay for it and have access to its features until their first renewal after August 17, 2025.
  • Advanced AI and Salesforce features are included in the new version of our Business+ plan and the new Enterprise+ plan. If you purchased Business+ on the Slack website, you’ll automatically switch to the new version of the plan at your first renewal after August 17, 2025.

** FAQs**

Why is Slack making these changes?

We have added significant new innovations and expanded the availability of existing features so that customers of all sizes, in all industries, can rely on Slack to run their businesses. To reflect new and added product functionality and to provide more of our customers with the opportunity to use them, we’re updating the features offered across our plans.

I signed a contract for my Business+ or Enterprise Grid plan with a Slack Account Executive. What do these changes mean for my organization?

Contact your AE for more details on how these changes may impact you, including options for renewing early to move to the new version of your current Business+ plan or the new Enterprise+ plan.

I’m currently paying for the Slack AI add-on, what can I expect?

If you purchased the Slack AI add-on from our website, you can continue using all AI features until your first renewal after August 17, 2025. Upon renewal, you’ll be moved to the new version of your paid plan and will have access to the AI features included in that plan. If you’re on Pro, this means that you’ll still be able to use conversation summaries and huddle notes, but would need to upgrade to Business+ in order to maintain access to other features like recaps, translations, and more.

How do I tell which version of the Slack plan I’m on?

To identify whether you’re on the latest version of your Slack Pro, Business+, or Enterprise plan, head to the AI feature access page. From the feature access page, you’ll be able to see which AI features you have access to (and which would become available with a switch to the new version of Business+ or the new Enterprise+ plan).

Where can I find my renewal date?

Workspace Owners on the Pro and Business+ plans can find their renewal date from the Billing page.

Can I restrict access to AI features for everyone in my workspace or organization?

Yes. Owners and admins can manage access permissions for each of our AI features, or turn them all off.

I don’t need to use AI features in Slack. Can I pay less if I turn them off?

No. While you can manage which AI features your members are able to use, the price you pay for your Slack plan won’t change if you turn all AI features off.

Updates to message and file history on free workspaces

Over the years, we’ve changed our plans and features to maintain the quality of Slack for our customers. As our customer base has continued to grow, so has our mission to make Slack a tool for businesses doing their best work.

We will be reducing our data storage offering for the free version of Slack. Starting August 26, 2024, we’ll begin deleting messages and files that are more than one year old from free workspaces on a rolling basis.

Changes for free workspaces

Slack will no longer keep messages and files for the lifetime of your free workspace. Starting August 26, 2024, Customer Data — such as messages and file history — older than one year may be deleted on a rolling basis from workspaces on the free plan, following the terms described in the Main Services Agreement and Trust and Compliance Documentation.

If you choose to remain on a free workspace, you’ll have full access to the past 90 days of message and file history, and the remaining 275 days will become available should you upgrade to a paid plan. If you decide to upgrade, we’ll store messages and files based on your chosen retention period, with an option to keep all history.

FAQs

When will my message and file history be deleted?

We’ll begin deleting any messages and files in your workspace older than one year on August 26, 2024. Going forward, this workspace data will be deleted on a continuous basis once it’s more than a year old.

Can I avoid losing my message and file history?

Existing free workspaces that upgrade to a paid plan before August 26, 2024 won’t be impacted.

My messages and files were deleted. Can they be recovered?

It will not be possible to restore messages and files once deletion occurs.

Can I export my workspace data?

Workspaces on the free version of Slack can export data. Visit Guide to Slack import and export tools for more details.

Will there be any changes to the 90-day message and file history access?

No. Workspaces on the free version of Slack will continue to have full access to the past 90 days of message and file history. To access message and file history beyond the 90-day limit, you’ll need to upgrade your workspace.

I downgraded from a paid plan, what will happen to my canvases and lists?

When you downgrade, your canvases become read only and subject to the 90-day limit. After a year, all canvas content will be deleted. Lists will not be visible when you downgrade to a free plan, but are stored should you decide to upgrade. After a year, list content is deleted and will not be restored if you upgrade.

Will there be any changes to message retention settings?

On the free version of Slack, you’ll have the option to choose whether messages and files (including canvases and lists) are deleted after 90 days, or whether messages and files are kept for a year. You will no longer have the option to keep messages or files for the lifetime of your workspace. If you work in Slack Connect channels with an Enterprise organization, messages and files in those channels will not be deleted if you set a one-year retention policy.

My workspace is part of the Slack for Nonprofits program. Will I be impacted?

The Slack for Nonprofits discount offers eligible workspaces a free or discounted upgrade to our Pro, Business+, or Enterprise plans. As long as you remain on one of our paid plans, your message and file history won’t be impacted.

I’m currently on a trial. What happens when my trial ends?

If you choose not to upgrade to a paid plan once your trial ends, the data in your workspace will be subject to our message and file deletion policy for free workspaces. If you upgrade your workspace when your trial ends, message and file history older than a year won’t be impacted.

What plans and features does Slack offer?

Visit our Pricing page to learn more about our plans and compare available features.

Use Channel Expert in Slack (legacy)

Note: As of May 4, 2026, it’s not possible to add Channel Expert to Slack. The below information is intended only for reference only. Check out Slackbot for a new way to use AI-powered agents in Slack.

Channel Expert is an AI-powered agent for Slack channels that can help answer frequently asked questions and funnel requests to internal subject matter experts if you need human assistance. Channel Expert uses generative AI and Slack data from the channel it’s been added to to answer your questions. For example, use Channel Expert in a channel dedicated to answering IT requests or questions about your company’s benefits coverage.

An GIF displaying Channel Expert functionality

Chat with Channel Expert

You can work with Channel Expert right in channels to get answers to questions. Anytime you mention Channel Expert in a channel it’s been added to, it’ll work with you to answer your question. Keep in mind, anyone with access to the channel will be able to see your question and the answers provided by Channel Expert.

  1. Open the channel where you’d like to message Channel Expert.
  2. Compose your message and make sure to mention Channel Expert by typing @channel expert to prompt them to answer.
  3. Send the message to start the conversation.

Channel Expert will reply to your question in thread. If you have a follow up question, mention Channel Expert again to continue the conversation.

Tip: You’ll see a banner above the message field in channels that Channel Expert has been added to.

Ask for human help

If configured by admins, you can request human assistance if Channel Expert’s answers are missing the mark. From a Channel Expert conversation, select Ask a human and your original question will be sent to a channel where people can help answer your question.

From a Channel Expert conversation, select Ask a human. Your original question will be forwarded to a channel where people can help answer your question.

Note: By default, Channel Expert will generate answers in English. Reach out to an admin to add support for additional languages.

Who can use this feature?

  • All members (but not guests)
  • Available on Business+ and Enterprise plans with a Salesforce Agentforce license

Verified organizations

Slack Connect is a secure way to collaborate with external organizations, right in Slack. Unlike email, which leaves your team at risk of spam and phishing, Slack Connect and verified organizations help ensure you’re working with trusted organizations.

What verification looks like

When Slack verifies an organization, a purple check mark will appear next to an organization’s name. Here are a few places where you can see this check mark:

  • When you add someone from a verified organization to a channel.
  • When you open a Slack Connect channel, click the channel name, then select the About or Settings tab to view a list of organizations in the channel.
  • When you accept an invite from someone at a verified organization.

Request from a member to join a channel with a verified company, showing a purple check mark next to the company name and buttons to approve or deny

How Slack verifies organizations

If verified, we’ll automatically apply the verified check mark to that organization’s profile. When evaluating the legitimacy of an organization, we look at a number of factors:

  • The organization is a paid customer of Slack.
  • The organization is authentic — it has a verifiable public business presence, or other factors we may evaluate.

Slack cannot fully guarantee that an organization’s identity is legitimate, and this feature is provided as a convenience for customers. It is ultimately the responsibility of customers to confirm the identity of its trusted external organizations. Slack is not liable for any issues caused by identification errors, and Slack reserves the right to remove the verified check mark from organizations at our discretion.

Note: Workspace Owners and Admins (Pro and Business+ plans) and Org Owners and Admins (Enterprise plans) can request to be verified by contacting our Support team.

Verify your identity in Slack

From time to time, our Support team will need to verify your identity in order to share information about your Slack account or workspace with you. Here’s how to verify your identity in Slack using the /verify shortcut.

GIF showing the verify shortcut being used in a channel

How it works

  • To verify your identity in Slack, you’ll use a built-in shortcut — /verify. Like all shortcuts, you’ll send the command in a channel or direct message (DM) in Slack.
  • Neither the shortcut you send nor the code you receive will be visible to anyone but you, so you can use /verify in any conversation in Slack without disrupting your team.

Verify your identity

  1. From your desktop, open a channel or DM.
  2. Click the message field.
  3. Type /verify, then press Enter to send the message. Make sure you include the forward slash at the beginning of your message.
  4. Copy the verification code displayed by Slackbot and include it in a reply to the Support team.

View and update Salesforce data in Slack

Spend less time switching between Slack and Salesforce by viewing and updating records right from your workspace. On Business+ and Enterprise plans, you can also create and update records with Slackbot (if you have access), view and share customized lists of records, and add dynamic Salesforce data to a canvas.

Note: Your Slack workspace must be on the new version of Business+ to access list views in Slack and add Salesforce data to a canvas. If you’re on Business+ and don’t see these features, reach out to our Support team.

Keep in mind

There are a few things you should know before getting using Salesforce data in Slack.

  • Field-level security determines what Salesforce data you can view or update in Slack.
  • You can only view certain supported objects in Slack or in list views.
  • Admins can choose which fields display when you view a record by configuring a Slack record layout.

Find and update a Salesforce record in Slack

Any updates you make to records (like accounts or opportunities) in Slack will be automatically reflected in Salesforce. Your permissions to view or edit a record in Slack match those set in Salesforce.

  1. Open the search field at the top of Slack.
  2. Type what you’re looking for into the search field, then choose the Search in Salesforce option in the search results drop-down menu.
  3. You’ll see a list of records that match your search. Select a record to view it in Slack. Update any fields you have permission to edit, then select Save Changes.

Note: If a record has a Salesforce channel associated with it, you can view and update record data, see related conversations, and participate in relevant conversions from the channel.

Create and update records with Slackbot

If you have access to Slackbot, you can ask it to find, create, or update Salesforce records in the flow of a conversation. Slackbot can only access Salesforce data you have permission to view or edit in any connected Salesforce orgs.

  1. From your desktop, click Slackbot at the top of the screen.
  2. Tell Slackbot what you’d like to do, ex. “Add [customer name] as a new contact” or “Update the next steps on [opportunity] based on my recent Slack messages and emails.”
  3. Slackbot will search Salesforce to find the right record to update, or create a new draft record. Before it makes any changes, you’ll be prompted to review and approve.

Tip: You can also ask Slackbot to attach uploaded files to Salesforce records.

Access list views

List views are collections of Salesforce records, typically organized by record type. On Business+ and Enterprise plans, you can access list views in Slack to view and update multiple records all in one place.

Desktop

Mobile

  1. From the Home tab, find the Salesforce section of your sidebar and select the Salesforce app.

  2. Select the List views tab.

  3. Search for and select a list view. From the list view, choose a record to view it in Slack, or click Share to send it to other people on your team.

  4. From the Home tab, tap the Salesforce app. Select the List views tab.

  5. Search for and select a list view.

  6. From the list view, choose a record to view it in Slack, or tap the ** three dots icon** and select Share in Slack to send it to other people on your team.

Tip: Click the star icon (or the emoji associated with a section) to move a list view to a custom section in your sidebar.

Add Salesforce data to a canvas

On Business+ and Enterprise plans, add Salesforce data to a canvas to ensure important information in your reports and other documents stays up to date. Any updates you make to record data anywhere in Slack or Salesforce is automatically reflected in Salesforce data you add to a canvas.

  1. From the Home tab, click Files.
  2. Click ** Canvases** in the left sidebar.
  3. Search for and select a canvas, or click New to create one.
  4. Click the plus button, then select Salesforce data field from the list.
  5. Select options for the required fields, then click Insert.

You’ll see Salesforce data in the canvas highlighted with a Salesforce icon. Click on any Salesforce data to view the record in Slack and update fields (if you have permission).

Who can use this feature?

  • All members with a connection to Salesforce
  • Available on all plans

Adjust your notifications

Configure your Slack notifications

Notifications in Slack keep you informed of the work you care about, whether you’re at your desk or on the move. Use the steps below to customize your desktop, mobile, and email notifications.

Note: If you’re having issues with notifications, visit Troubleshoot Slack notifications for help.

How notifications work

  • By default, you’ll receive notifications on desktop and mobile (if you’ve downloaded the Slack iOS or Android app).
  • You can decide whether you receive banner notifications on desktop or mobile, and adjust your default settings to be notified about Everything or ** Mentions and direct messages**.
  • If you choose to only be notified about mentions and direct messages (DMs), you can set exceptions to be notified about everything in certain channels or DMs.

Choose how you’re notified

Adjust your notification preferences to decide where you receive banner notifications and whether you’re notified about all messages or only mentions and DMs.

Desktop

Mobile

  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app

  2. Select Preferences then click Notifications.

  3. Below How to notify you, check or uncheck the box next to Desktop notifications or Mobile notifications.

  4. Select Everything or Mentions and direct messages from the What to notify you about drop-down menu.

  5. Download the Slack app to your mobile device and sign in to your workspace (if you haven’t already).

  6. Tap your profile picture at the top of the screen, then tap ** Notifications**.

  7. Tap the toggle next to Mobile notifications if they aren’t turned on.

  8. Below What to notify you about, select Everything or Mentions and direct messages.

Set mobile overrides and additional notification preferences

You can set a different notification preference for mobile and choose whether or not you’re notified in the following scenarios:

  • Someone replies to a thread you’re following
  • You receive a message from a VIP when your notifications are paused or you’re in focus mode (paid plans only)
  • A huddle starts in one of your channels or DMs

  5. Tap your profile picture at the top of the screen, then tap ** Notifications**.

  6. Below Also notify you about, tap the toggle next to an option.

Tip: If you only want to receive notifications during certain hours or on certain days, you can set a notification schedule. Outside of the schedule you set, your notifications will be paused.

Choose what to show in Activity

Activitynotifications appear as a numbered badge in the sidebar. You’ll always see DMs, mentions, reactions, and thread replies, but you can choose whether to see other types of notifications in Activity as well:

  • Channels with notifications set to “All new posts”
  • Reminders when Later item due dates arrive

Desktop

Mobile

Set up keyword notifications

You can set keywords to receive notifications about topics that are important to you. Whenever someone uses one of your keywords in a channel you’ve joined, you’ll get a notification and see the keyword highlighted in yellow.

Guide to Slack notifications

Notifications in Slack are designed to keep you informed, whether you’re at your desk or on the go. Read on to learn more about Slack notifications and how they work.

Tip: Visit our other articles to learn how to configure your notifications and troubleshoot notifications.

Notifications overview

You’ll receive desktop notifications when you’re using Slack on your computer. When you’re away from your desk, you’ll receive notifications from your Slack mobile app or by email. Here’s when you’ll receive notifications by default:

  • Someone sends you a direct message (DM)
  • Someone replies to a thread you’re following
  • Someone mentions you, notifies a channel you’re in, or uses one of your keywords

These defaults apply to both desktop and mobile notifications unless you adjust your preferences.

Desktop notifications

Whether you’ve downloaded the Slack desktop app or use Slack in a browser, you’ll receive banner, sidebar, and app icon notifications to let you know about unread activity in Slack.

Banner notifications

Banner notifications alert you of new activity in Slack, including who sent a message and in which conversation. From your preferences, you can choose a sound for banner notifications and whether to include a preview of messages.

Sidebar notifications

When there’s unread activity in a conversation, the conversation name will appear bold in your sidebar. You’ll also see a numbered badge if someone mentions you. When you open the conversation, the mention will be highlighted in the message so that you can easily see what needs your attention.

Workspace icon notifications

If you’re signed into more than one workspace on the desktop app, you’ll see a numbered badge on your workspace icon when there’s unread activity in your other workspaces. Click the workspace icon to see a list of your signed-in workspaces, and look for a numbered badge to learn which one has unread activity.

App icon notifications

You’ll receive badge notifications on the Slack app icon when you have unread activity. The appearance and placement of these notifications vary by operating system:

Mac

Windows

Linux

By default, any unread activity will display a red badge on the Slack icon.

  • • A dot means you have unread activity in one of your Slack workspaces.
  • 3 A number means someone sent you a direct message, mentioned you, notified a channel you’re in, used one of your keywords, or replied to a thread you’re following.

On Windows, you’ll see badge notifications in two places: in your taskbar and in your notifications area.

Taskbar

In your taskbar, a red badge means someone sent you a direct message, mentioned you, used one of your keywords or replied to a thread you’re following. If your taskbar is set to small taskbar buttons, badges on the Slack icon will not be visible.

Notifications area

When Slack is running, you’ll see a Slack icon in your notifications area.

  • Windows_notification_tray_blue_badge.png – A blue badge means you have unread activity in one of your workspaces.
  • Windows_notification_tray_red_badge.png – A red badge means someone sent you a direct message, mentioned you, used one of your keywords, or replied to a thread you’re following.

On Linux, you’ll see badge notifications in your notifications area when the Slack app is running.

  • Windows_notification_tray_blue_badge.png – A blue badge means you have unread activity in one of your workspaces.
  • Windows_notification_tray_red_badge.png – A red badge means a someone sent you a direct message, mentioned you, used one of your keywords, or replied to a thread you’re following.

Mobile notifications

To receive notifications on your mobile device, download the Slack app and sign in to your workspace. Here’s how they work:

  • You can choose whether to receive notifications on mobile, and choose to be notified differently than you are on desktop.
  • Adjust your notification preferences to receive mobile notifications as soon as a message is sent, as soon as you’re inactive on desktop, or after an additional delay.
  • When there are unread messages (DMs, mentions, or keywords), you’ll see a badge on the Slack app icon.

Note: Conversations with unread activity will appear bold at the top of the channel list in the Home tab of your Slack mobile app.

Email notifications

By default, you’ll receive email notifications when you join a Slack workspace and haven’t enabled mobile notifications. When you’re not active in Slack, you can receive email notifications to alert you of mentions, DMs, and replies to threads you’re following. These notifications are bundled and sent once every 15 minutes or once an hour, depending on your preferences.

Tip: You can reply to a Slack message from any email notification.

Manage notifications for specific channels and direct messages

Notifications in Slack are designed to keep you informed whether you’re at your desk or on the go. To get notifications about the things you care about most, you can set notification preferences for specific channels and direct messages (DMs) with three or more people.

Configure conversation-specific notifications

You can choose to be notified about all new posts or just mentions in channels and group DMs. To turn off notifications for a conversation entirely, you can mute it.

Desktop

Mobile

  1. Open a channel or group DM.

  2. Click the Notifications icon at the top of the conversation and select All new posts or Just mentions.

  3. From a channel or group DM, tap the conversation name.

  4. Tap Settings & Details.

  5. Tap Notifications.

  6. Choose your preference for the conversation.

Set additional conversation-specific notification preferences

If you’d like, you can choose from the following options to further customize notifications for certain channels or DMs:

  • Desktop notifications See a banner on your desktop when you get a notification.
  • Mobile notifications See a banner on your mobile device when you get a notification.
  • Get different notifications on mobile Choose a different notification option for mobile.
  • Badge every unread message Show a badge in your sidebar for every new message.
  • Follow every thread Get notified about every new thread and any replies.

Desktop

Mobile

  1. Open a channel or group DM.

  2. Click the Notifications icon at the top of the conversation and select Advanced options.

  3. Click the toggle next to the settings you’d like to change.

  4. From a channel or group DM, tap the conversation name.

  5. Tap Settings & Details.

  6. Tap Notifications.

  7. Tap the toggle next to the settings you’d like to change.

Review conversation-specific notifications

You can view a list of channels and group DMs with conversation-specific notification settings (including muted conversations) from your preferences.

Desktop

Mobile

  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app

  2. Select Preferences, then click Notifications.

  3. Scroll down to Exceptions to the defaults.

  4. Click the megaphone, mention, or mute icon to adjust the notification settings for a conversation, or click the close icon to reset notifications back to the default setting.

  5. Tap your profile picture at the top of the screen, then tap Notifications.

  6. Below Exceptions to the defaults, tap Channels or Direct messages.

  7. Tap a conversation to adjust the settings.

Manage your Slack email subscriptions

From time to time, we’ll send you emails. This might include news about Slack apps and features, opportunities to provide feedback, or Slack tips. You can manage these email subscriptions from your preferences.

Update your email preferences

  1. From your desktop, navigate to the Notifications tab in your Account settings by following this link: 0
  2. Under Email News and Updates, check the boxes next to the types of emails you’d like to receive. Uncheck the boxes next to the types of emails you don’t want to receive.

Note: If you opt out of the all of the email types listed, we’ll still send you important administrative emails, such as password resets.

Configure your email notifications

You can choose to receive Slack notifications by email, as well as manage what you get notified about and how often you receive them. Email notifications are bundled and can be delivered every 15 minutes or once an hour.

  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Select Preferences, then click Notifications.
  3. Under When I’m not active on desktop, check or uncheck the box next to Send me email notifications for mentions and direct messages. If checked, choose how often you’d like notifications delivered.

Mute channels and direct messages

You can mute specific channels and direct messages (DMs) if you don’t want to get notifications for those conversations. While muted conversations are typically hidden from your sidebar, you’ll still see these sidebar notifications:

  • Numbered badges will appear next to conversations if you’re mentioned or receive a DM.
  • At the top of your sidebar, Threads will appear bold if someone replies to a message you’ve sent in a muted conversation.

Tip: Adjust your preferences to show or hide muted conversations in your sidebar.

Mute a channel

Desktop

Mobile

  6. Select Mute channel.

Desktop

Mobile

Mute a DM with an app or bot

Apps and bots connected to your workspace can send you messages in dedicated DMs. To mute a DM with an app or bot, use the steps below:

Desktop

Mobile

Temporarily mute a channel

You can mute a channel for a short period of time — either one hour or until tomorrow.

  1. From your desktop, open the channel you’d like to mute.
  2. Click the Notifications icon at the top of the channel.
  3. Hover over More options, and under Temporarily mute… choose how long you want to mute notifications.

Pause your Slack notifications

If you need time to focus or time away from work, you can pause your notifications in Slack. Pause notifications as needed to help you concentrate, or set a notification schedule for routine times you’d prefer not to be interrupted.

How it works

  • You won’t receive any notifications. Once you resume notifications, you can review any messages you received while you weren’t actively looking at Slack.
  • Other people will see a snooze icon next to your name. When sending a direct message (DM), they can override this setting to notify you about an urgent message once per day.

Tip: To pause notifications while also reducing sidebar distractions, try focus mode.

Set a notification schedule

For the times you’re routinely offline, you can set a notification schedule. With a schedule in place, you’ll only receive notifications on days you choose during certain hours. Outside of those times, notifications will be paused.

Mobile

Shortcuts and commands

Short on time? Use a slash command to quickly pause or resume your notifications.

  • Action – /dnd example
  • Pause notifications for a specific amount of time – /dnd for 15 mins /dnd 15 minutes
  • Pause notifications until a specific time – /dnd until 17:00 /dnd until 5pm
  • Pause notifications until a time of day – /dnd until tonight /dnd until tomorrow morning
  • Resume notifications – /dnd off

Who can use this feature?

  • All members
  • Available on all plans

Troubleshoot Slack notifications

Having problems with Slack notifications? Use this article to troubleshoot issues on your computer or mobile device.

Tip: To learn how to adjust your notification preferences, visit Configure your Slack notifications. If you’re having trouble with email notifications, check out Trouble receiving emails from Slack.

An overview of notification issues

  • Issue – Description
  • Stuck badge notifications or bolded Threads view – Badges 3 don’t clear or your Threads view stays bolded after you’ve caught up on your conversations.
  • Not receiving notifications – Notifications you’re expecting aren’t delivered.
  • Delayed notifications – Notifications that show up slower than you expect.
  • No notification sounds – Notifications that are delivered without a sound playing.

Stuck notifications or unread threads

If you see notification badges for conversations you’ve already read or your Threads view won’t unbold, something might be out of sync on our end.

Desktop

iOS

Android

Mark everything as read
  1. From the Slack desktop app or Slack in a browser, open the affected workspace.
  2. Press Shift Esc.

If marking everything as read doesn’t resolve the issue, you can contact us for more help. Please be sure to include a brief summary of the issue as well as your workspace URL and email address in the request.

Mark everything as read on desktop
  1. From the Slack desktop app, open the affected workspace.
  2. Press Shift Esc.
Clear the Slack app cache
  1. Tap your profile picture at the top of the screen, then tap Preferences.
  2. Below Device & Troubleshooting, tap Debug & Reset Cache.
  3. Tap Reset Cache.
Clear app data from your device settings

In addition to clearing the Slack app cache, you can also clear the app data from your device.

  1. Open Settings on your device.
  2. Scroll down to Slack in the list of apps.
  3. Tap the toggle next to Reset Cache on Next Launch.
  4. Open the app to reset the cache.

Note: This will log you out of all workspaces you’re signed in to.

Mark everything as read on desktop
  1. From the Slack desktop app, open the affected workspace.
  2. Press Shift Esc.
Clear the Slack app cache
  1. Tap your profile picture at the top of the screen, then tap Preferences.
  2. Tap Reset Cache.
Clear app data from your device settings

In addition to clearing the Slack app cache, you can also clear the app data from your device.

  1. Open Settings on your device.
  2. Tap Apps.
  3. Tap the Slack icon.
  4. Tap Storage.
  5. Tap Clear Data.

Note: This will log you out of all workspaces you’re signed in to.

Not receiving notifications

System settings can sometimes interfere with Slack notification delivery. If you’re not receiving notifications, give these steps a try.

Tip: Make sure you haven’t paused notifications in Slack. If you see a snooze icon next to your name, visit Pause your Slack notifications to learn how to resume notifications.

Mac

Windows

Browser

iOS

Android

Check your macOS notification preferences
  1. Open your computer’s System Preferences, then click Notifications.
  2. Make sure the when mirroring or sharing the display setting is enabled.
  3. Next, select Slack from the list of applications.
  4. Make sure the Allow Notifications from Slack toggle is on and your alert style is set to either Banners or Alerts.
Check your macOS Do Not Disturb settings
  1. Click the toggles icon in the top right corner of your screen to open the Mac Control Center.
  2. Click Do Not Disturb and make sure it’s toggled off.
Check your settings for Notifications & Actions
  1. On Windows 10, click the Start menu.
  2. Select Settings, then System.
  3. From the left sidebar, click Notifications & Actions.
  4. Ensure Get notifications from apps and other senders is enabled.
  5. Find Slack in the list and check if notifications are enabled.
Check your Focus Assist settings
  1. On Windows 10, click the Start menu.
  2. Select Settings, then System.
  3. From the left sidebar, click Focus Assist.
  4. Select Off to deactivate Focus Assist and resume receiving notifications.

Note: If notification sounds stop working on Windows 10, check to make sure Windows Quiet Hours are not active.

Chrome
  1. From the Chrome menu at the top of your screen, select Preferences.
  2. Click Privacy and security in the left sidebar, then click Site Settings.
  3. Below Permissions, select Notifications.
  4. Make sure Sites can ask to send notifications is toggled on.
Edge
  1. From the Edge menu at the top of your screen, click the three dots icon.
  2. Click Cookies and site permissions in the left sidebar.
  3. Below All permissions, select Notifications.
  4. Make sure Slack is included in the Allow section.
Firefox
  1. From the Firefox menu at the top of your screen, select Preferences.
  2. Click Privacy & Security in the left sidebar.
  3. Below Permissions, click the Settings button next to Notifications.
  4. Make sure your Slack workspace is included in the Notifications Permissions list.
Safari
  1. From the Safari menu at the top of your screen, select Preferences.
  2. Click Websites, then select Notifications from the left sidebar.
  3. Make sure your Slack workspace is allowed to send notifications.

Note: You’ll only get notifications for workspaces that you have open in your browser.

Tip: Power saving mode or performance optimization apps may also prevent Slack from sending notifications. If using one of these, try deactivating it or adding Slack to its allowlist.

Force quit the app and restart your device

Sometimes notification issues can be fixed by restarting your phone or tablet.

Run a test to identify issues

If restarting your device didn’t fix the problem, you can run a diagnostic test from the app. Depending on the results of the test, there may be additional troubleshooting steps you can try.

  1. Tap your profile picture at the top of the screen, then tap Notifications.
  2. Tap Troubleshoot Notifications.
Fix issues from the test

If the first four parts of the test pass but you don’t receive a test notification, try uninstalling and reinstalling the Slack app on your device, then re-run the test. If that doesn’t help, restart your device again.

Note: If running the test doesn’t reveal any issues or the steps above don’t fix the problem, run the test again and tap Send a report so our Support team can help out.

Tip: Power saving mode or performance optimization apps may also prevent Slack from sending notifications. If using one of these, try deactivating it or adding Slack to its allowlist.

Force quit the app and restart your device

Sometimes notification issues can be fixed by restarting your phone or tablet.

Check your Google Play Services settings
  1. Open the Settings app on your Android device.
  2. Click Application manager, then locate Google Play Services.
  3. Make sure Show notifications is checked.

Note: Google Play Services is required to receive notifications on Android. Make sure your device is supported.

Run a test to identify issues

If restarting your device didn’t fix the problem, you can run a diagnostic test from the app. Depending on the results of the test, there may be additional troubleshooting steps you can try.

  1. Tap your profile picture at the top of the screen, then tap Notifications.
  2. Tap Troubleshoot Notifications.
Fix issues from the test

Try restarting your device again, then resetting the cache. If that doesn’t work, you can uninstall and reinstall the Slack app.

Note: If running the test doesn’t reveal any issues or the steps above don’t fix the problem, run the test again and tap Send a report so our Support team can help out.

Connect Slackbot to other apps with MCP

Connect Slackbot to other apps you use to take actions in those apps directly from Slack. When you install an app that includes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, anyone with access to Slackbot can interact with other services just by starting a conversation.

How it works

  • Developers (either third-party developers or developers at your organization) can add MCP servers to Slack apps they build. When you install an app, Slackbot gains access to a set of tools configured by the developer to take actions in that app from Slack.
  • If app approval is required in your workspace or Enterprise organization, only admins and members with permission can install apps that include MCP servers.
  • As with other apps, members need to connect their accounts in order to use them. When a member connects their account, Slackbot will have access to all of the tools built into the MCP server.

Available apps

The apps listed below include MCP servers you can connect to Slackbot:

  • Amplitude
  • Amplitude - EU
  • Atlassian Rovo
  • Bob
  • Box
  • Brex
  • Canva
  • Docusign
  • Figma
  • Gamma
  • Ironclad
  • Linear
  • Lucidchart
  • Lucidspark
  • Miro
  • Reclaim.ai (by Dropbox)
  • Replit
  • Vercel
  • Webflow
  • Zoom

More apps will be available soon, so keep an eye on the Slack Marketplace for an up-to-date list.

Tip: Head to the Slack developer docs for instructions on adding an MCP server to your own app.

Install an app

Install an app to connect its MCP server with Slackbot. If you already have an app that now includes an MCP server installed, add the new version. Any members who want to continue using the app will need to re-connect their accounts once the new version is installed.

Pro, Business+, and Enterprise Select

Enterprise Grid and Enterprise+

If app approval is turned on for your workspace, Workspace Owners and Admins can install apps and approve app requests submitted by members.

  1. Open the Slack Marketplace and find the app you’d like to install.
  2. Click Add to Slack.
  3. Follow the prompts to review the scopes and install the app. Any MCP servers will be listed below Actions [app] can take.

Org Owners and Org Admins can install apps at the org level. Once you’ve installed an app, you can add it to workspaces and set access permissions for specific users and groups.

Install an app
  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Hover over Tools & settings, then click Organization settings.
  3. From the left sidebar, click Integrations.
  4. Click Manage Apps in the top right, then select Install an app.
  5. Search for and select the app you’d like to install.
  6. Click Continue.
  7. Follow the prompts to review the scopes and install the app. Any MCP servers will be listed below Actions [app] can take.
Add an app to workspaces
  1. From the Integrations section of the admin dashboard, click Installed apps.
  2. Find the app you’d like to add to workspaces.
  3. Click the three dots icon to the right of the app.
  4. Select Add to more workspaces.
  5. Check the box next to any workspaces you’d like to add the app to. To automatically add the app to any new workspaces created in your org, check the box next to Default for future workspaces.
  6. Click Next.
  7. Check the box next to I’m ready to add this app.
  8. Click Add App.
Set access permissions
  1. From the Integrations section of the admin dashboard, click Installed apps.
  2. Select an app from the list, then click the Member Permissions tab at the top of the page.
  3. Next to Who has permission to initiate interaction with this app, click Edit.
  4. Choose who can use the app — Everyone, No one, or Specific people and groups. If you select Specific people and groups, add members, IDP groups, or user groups.
  5. Click Save.

Manage MCP server access

Org Owners and Org Admins on the Enterprise Grid and Enterprise+ plans can manage access to MCP servers once an app is installed.

  1. From the Integrations section of the admin dashboard, click Installed apps.
  2. Select an app from the list, then click the Member Permissions tab at the top of the page.
  3. Below MCP servers, click Edit next to an MCP server.
  4. Choose who can access the MCP server — Everyone, Everyone with app access except specific people or groups, Only specific people or groups with app access, or No one. If you select Everyone except specific people or groups or Only specific people or groups, pick members, IDP groups, or user groups.
  5. Click Save.

Note: It’s not possible to manage MCP server access on the Pro, Business+, or Enterprise Select plans.

Who can use this feature?

  • Org Owners/Admins (Enterprise Grid and Enterprise+), Workspace Owners/Admins (Pro, Business+, and Enterprise Select), and members with permission to install apps

Connect Slackbot to Salesforce with MCP

Add and configure Salesforce Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers in Slack to connect Slackbot with Salesforce or Data 360. When you add an MCP server, members of your workspace or Enterprise organization can use Slackbot to take actions in Salesforce without leaving Slack.

How it works

  • When you set up and configure an MCP server in Slack, members can access information and take actions in Salesforce just by starting a conversation with Slackbot.
  • In order to set up and configure a Salesforce MCP server, you’ll need to connect at least one Salesforce org to Slack.
  • Once you’ve connected Slack and Salesforce, choose one or more standard MCP servers to allow Slackbot access to Salesforce or Data Cloud.
  • Developers in your organization can build custom MCP servers to give Slackbot access to additional tools via Apex Actions, Lightning Flows, Apex REST endpoints, APIs from the API Catalog, Prompt Builder templates, and Agentforce agents.

Salesforce MCP servers

You can choose from a list of standard Salesforce MCP servers.

  • Server name – Server description

  • Data 360 – Supports SQL queries across Data Cloud, including CRM, Commerce Cloud, Marketing Cloud, and external data sources

  • SObject All –

    Supports full CRUD functionality for Salesforce objects:

    • Create
    • Read
    • Update
    • Delete
    • Query
    • Search
    • Traverse relationships

  • SObject Deletes – Supports delete actions for records with dependency awareness

  • SObject Mutations – Supports create and update actions for Salesforce records

  • SObject Reads – Supports search and retrieval for Salesforce records using SOQL

  • Tableau Next – Provides access to business intelligence (ex., dashboards, KPIs, and other data) through the Tableau semantic layer

Guide to AI features in Slack

Slack offers built-in generative AI tools backed by your conversation data to help any team work more productively. Our native AI features are intuitive, secure, and tailored to your organization.

Looking for information about the new version of Slackbot? Head to A reintroduction to Slackbot for all the details.

What to expect

  • The AI features available to you depend on your Slack plan, your role (member or guest), and whether your admins have restricted access.
  • AI-generated responses will only include information available to you (ex., messages and other content from public channels, private channels you belong to, and your direct messages).
  • Slack is committed to data security and privacy, and upholding these commitments is fundamental to everything we do. Visit Security for AI features in Slack for an overview.

Feature availability by plan

  • Feature – Pro – Business+ – Enterprise+
  • Conversation summaries – ✓ – ✓ – ✓
  • Huddle notes – ✓ – ✓ – ✓
  • Automatic search filters – ✓ – ✓ – ✓
  • Search answers – ✓ – ✓
  • Recaps – ✓ – ✓
  • File summaries – ✓ – ✓
  • Translations – ✓ – ✓
  • Workflow automation – ✓ – ✓
  • Message explanations – ✓ – ✓
  • Canvas content generation – ✓ – ✓
  • Slackbot – ✓ – ✓
  • Enterprise search – ✓

Note: If you’re on the legacy version of Business+ or the Enterprise Grid plan without the Slack AI add-on, you’ll only have access to the Pro features listed above. For more details, visit Updates to feature availability and pricing for Slack plans.

Summarize conversations

Get up to speed more quickly in any channel, direct message (DM), or thread. Whether you’re joining a new channel, returning from time off, or catching up on a fast-moving discussion, AI can summarize conversations in seconds.

Generating a summary with Slack AI

Summarize a channel or DM

You can summarize just your unread messages, the last seven days, or a custom date range (desktop only).

Desktop

Mobile

  1. Open the channel or DM you’d like to summarize.

  2. Click the three dots icon at the top of the conversation and select Summarize channel or Summarize conversation.

  3. Choose an option to generate your summary, which will appear when it’s ready.

  4. If you’d like, click the ** More details** icon to view the summary’s sources.

  5. Open the channel or DM you’d like to summarize.

  6. Tap Summarize in the top right.

  7. Choose an option to generate your summary. When it’s ready, you’ll see a badge on the Summarize icon. Tap it to view your summary.

Summarize a thread

Desktop

Mobile

  2. Click the Summarize button at the top of the thread. Your summary will appear when it’s ready.

  3. If you’d like, click the More details icon to view the summary’s sources.

  4. Open the thread you’d like to summarize.

  5. Tap Summarize in the top right.

  6. When your summary is ready, you’ll see a badge on the Summarize icon. Tap it to view your summary.

Automatic search filtering

  3. Next to ** Search details** at the top of the search results page, you’ll see which filters were applied. Click ** Filters** to adjust the results, or enter another search to try again.

Ask a question in your own words and get a concise answer based on relevant information in Slack, rather than sifting through search results.

Searching for the answer to a question with Slack AI

Desktop

Mobile

  2. Type your question and press Enter.

  3. AI answers will appear at the top of your search results. Answers include citations that refer to the source messages or files that informed them. Hover over a citation to preview the source, or click on it to view the message or file.

  4. To share a helpful answer with others, click ** Share. Review the answer, then click Share anyway** to send it to a channel or DM.

  5. Tap the search bar at the top of Slack.

  6. Type your question and tap Search or the magnifying glass icon on your device’s keyboard

  7. AI answers will appear at the top of your search results. Answers include citations that refer to the source messages or files that informed them, and you can tap a citation to view the sources.

Tip: If you’re on the Enterprise+ plan, an Org Owner or Admin can enable enterprise search to include content and information from other sources (like Google Drive, GitHub, and more) in search results.

Recap what you missed

Get caught up after some time away from Slack with a customized summary of your unread channels. With recaps, you can get automated daily summaries for channels that you’re interested in keeping tabs on but don’t want to interrupt you throughout your workday.

Adding channels to a Slack AI recap

  • When you set up your recap for the first time, Slack will recommend a few channels that you visit often, but don’t tend to participate in, that you might want to include.
  • Once you review which channels to include and turn recaps on, you can mute those channels to keep your sidebar tidy, or unmute the conversations you’d like to continue keeping a closer eye on.
  • You’ll get a new recap every morning with what you missed from the previous day. If you’re away for a longer period of time, your recap will cover however many days you were gone.
  • If you open your recap more than once a day, you can refresh to see any new updates.

Guide to Model Context Protocol in Slack

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open-source framework for connecting AI applications with other software systems. You can use the Slack MCP server to connect AI tools to Slack, or set Slackbot up as an MCP client so it can take actions in other apps.

How MCP works in Slack

  • The Slack MCP server provides AI assistants with secure access to your Slack workspace or Enterprise organization, allowing them to interact with your organization’s data.
  • You can also set Slackbot up as an MCP client. Install an app with an MCP server to connect Slackbot to that app, or choose from a variety of Salesforce servers.

Note: The following applications are considered non-SFDC Applications as defined in Salesforce’s Main Services Agreement.

Slack MCP server

The Slack MCP server lets third-party AI assistants like Claude and Perplexity securely access your Slack content so they can search messages, find information, and take actions in Slack on your behalf.

To get started, choose from our partner apps and follow their setup instructions to install and connect them to the Slack MCP server. Once connected, third-party AI assistants can access your Slack workspace to read specific channels or threads, send messages, create canvases, and help you find information faster.

What AI assistants can do

The MCP server provides tools for the following actions:

  • Search throughout Slack Search for messages, files, members, and channels.
  • Retrieve and send messages Read and retrieve channel history and send messages to any type of conversation in Slack.
  • Manage canvases Create and read Slack canvases.
  • Access member info Access and read profile information including custom profile fields and statuses.
MCP server partner apps

Get started using the Slack MCP server by setting up a connection with an available partner:

  • ChatGPT
  • Claude
  • Credal AI
  • Cursor
  • Dropbox
  • Guru
  • Jasper
  • Notion
  • Open AI
  • Perplexity
  • Thoughtspot
  • Wordsmith
  • Workleap

Note: This is a general overview of the Slack MCP server. For more detailed information and guidance on how to develop your own MCP client, read the Slack MCP server overview in our developer docs.

Slackbot MCP client

An MCP client can establish a secure connection with one or more MCP servers. Connect Slackbot with other apps so it can access information and take action on your members’ behalf.

When you install apps that include an MCP server to your Slack workspace or Enterprise organization, anyone with access to Slackbot can interact with those apps just by starting a conversation.

What Slackbot can do

Developers decide which tools to build into their MCP server for Slackbot to use, so the actions Slackbot can take depend on the app it’s connected to and the tools available. Typically, apps offer a set of read tools (so Slackbot can search for information and return relevant results) and a set of write tools (for Slackbot to create a new document or update existing content).
