Reserved names

There are several words that we reserve to avoid confusion in Slack, and can’t be used in full names or display names:

  • Brazilian Portuguese: aqui, canais, canal, eu, general, geral, grupo, meu, todos
  • Chinese (Simplified): 归档, 已归档, 全部, 频道, 创建, 删除, 已删除的频道, 编辑, 所有人, 组, 在线, 我, Slack, slackbot, 今天, 你
  • Chinese (Traditional): 全部, 頻道, 茶水間, 我, 您, 公開區, Slackbot, slack, 所有人, 這裡
  • English: archive, archived, archives, all, channel, channels, create, delete, deleted-channel, edit, everyone, general, group, groups, here, ja, me, ms, slack, slackbot, today, you
  • French: chaîne/chaine, canal, général/general, groupe, ici, moi, tous
  • German: alle, allgemein, Channel/channel, hier, Gruppe/gruppe, mir
  • Italian: tutti, canale, gruppo, qui, me, tu
  • Japanese: チャンネル, ここ, 全員, 自分, グループ, general
  • Korean: 여기, 모두, 전체, 모든, 전부, 채널, 나, 그룹
  • Spanish: aquí, canal, general, grupo, mí, todos

Change your email address

The email address you use for Slack is where we’ll send password reset emails and other important communications — it’s best to keep up to date.

Update your email address

Desktop

Mobile

  1. From your desktop, navigate to your Account settings by following this link: 0.

  2. Next to Email Address, click Expand.

  3. Enter your password and new email address, then click Update Email.

  4. Check the confirmation email in your new email inbox with the subject line Confirm your new email address.

  5. Open the email, then click Confirm your email address.

  6. The confirmation link will take you to your Account page in a browser. If you’re prompted to sign-in to Slack, use your old email address to sign-in.

  7. Next to Email Address, click Expand to see your updated email address, then click Save.

  8. Open your mobile web browser and go to my.slack.com/account/settings.

  9. By Email Address, tap expand.

  10. Enter your current password and new email address. Double-check that you’ve spelled the email address correctly.

  11. Tap Update Email.

  12. Check the confirmation email in your new email inbox with the subject line Confirm your new email address.

  13. Open the email and tap Confirm your email address.

    The confirmation link will take you to your Account page in a browser. From there, you’ll see your new, confirmed email address in the Email Address section to save it. If you’re not signed in to Slack when you click Confirm your email address, use your old email address to sign in to save the change.

Note: If your Workspace Owner has enabled single sign-on, your ability to edit personal information, including email addresses, may be restricted.

Update your email on multiple workspaces

You can use the same email address to join or create multiple workspaces, but your account for each workspace is separate. To change your email address for another Slack workspace, sign in and repeat the same steps above.

** Missing confirmation emails**

We’ll send a confirmation email shortly after you update your email address. If you didn’t receive the email, try the following:

  • Check your spam or junk folder, and any filters in your inbox.
  • Open your email settings and check for typos in the email address. If the address is incorrect, you can change it by following the steps above.

Still having trouble? Contact us and tell us how we can help.

Tip: If your workspace allows, your email address may be visible in your profile. If so, other members can search for you with that email address.

Change your Slack theme

Change the appearance of your workspace by choosing a new theme, or create a custom theme with the colors of your choice.

Tip: If you’d like a darker look for Slack, you can turn on dark mode from your preferences or temporarily turn on focus mode.

Color_Theming_HC.gif Choose a new theme

If you use multiple workspaces, try selecting a different theme for each one to help tell them apart. Your new theme will appear whenever you open Slack on any device or in your browser.

  1. From your desktop, click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Select Preferences from the menu.
  3. Click Themes.
  4. Below Slack themes, select an option.

Note: Some people with colorblindness have found our vision assistive themes helpful. We’re always working to make Slack more accessible and listening to feedback about how we can improve themes.

Create a custom theme

Set custom colors
  1. From your desktop, click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Select Preferences from the menu.
  3. Click Appearance, then select Custom theme.
  4. For each element, select a swatch from the color picker.
  5. Click the close icon, then click Save changes.
Share your theme

Your custom theme will only be visible to you. If you’d like to showcase it, you can share your color selection with others.

  1. From your desktop, click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Select Preferences from the menu.
  3. Click Appearance, then select Custom theme.
  4. Next to Theme Colors, click Share to copy your theme.
  5. Navigate to any conversation and paste your theme into a message, then press Enter to send it. Any member of that conversation can select Apply Slack theme to use it themselves.
Import your legacy theme

To apply the colors from the theme you last used before Slack was updated to the new design, you can import your legacy theme.

  1. From your desktop, click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Select Preferences from the menu.
  3. Click Appearance, then select Custom theme.
  4. Next to Theme Colors, click Import theme.
  5. Click Paste your legacy theme colors, then click Apply.
Set theme preferences

You can set two other preferences to further adjust the look of your theme:

  • Window gradient Decide whether your windows are a solid color or have a gradient.
  • Darker sidebars By default, some themes have a darker sidebar. If you pick a theme with a light sidebar, you can adjust the contrast with the Darker sidebars preference.
  1. From your desktop, click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Select Preferences from the menu.
  3. Click Appearance, then click Custom theme.
  4. Check the box next to the preference(s) you’d like to set, then click Save.

Tip: On certain Mac devices, you can turn window transparency off from the Accessibility section of your preferences.

Choose how member names appear for you in Slack

From your preferences, you can choose how members’ names appear in Slack. Keep in mind that this preference only affects what you’ll see. Using the steps below, select from one of these options:

  • Full & display names Show display names in messages, and full names everywhere else.
  • Just display names Show display names everywhere in Slack.

Set your preference for member names

Desktop

iOS

  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. A cursor over the profile picture menu in the Slack desktop app.

  2. Select Preferences.

  3. Select Messages & media.

  4. Under Names, choose how you’d like to see members’ names.

  5. Tap your profile picture at the top of your screen.

  6. Tap Preferences.

  7. Under Appearance, tap Message Display.

  8. Tap the toggle next to Display Full Names on or off.

Note: This preference isn’t available on the Slack Android app.

Customize the Slack mobile app

On the Slack mobile app, you can customize what appears along the top of your app so you can quickly access what’s most important to you.

Customize the top of your mobile app

Show, hide, or re-order the items that appear at the top of your Home tab, like Catch up, Threads, Drafts & sent, and Recap.

  1. From the Home tab, swipe left on the existing items, then tap the settings icon.
  2. Tap the toggle next to the items you’d like to show or hide.
  3. To reorder the items, press and hold the six dots icon, then drag the item to a new position.

Tip: Tap and hold any item to re-order it from the Home tab.

Sort your conversation list

The Home tab contains a list of your conversations, similar to the sidebar on desktop. By default, conversations on mobile will be sorted alphabetically, or by section if you use custom sections. You can choose to sort by recent activity instead.

Manage your haptic feedback preference

On an iOS device, you can decide whether you feel haptic feedback when tapping buttons in the Slack mobile app.

  1. Tap your profile picture in the top-right corner of the Slack app.
  2. Select Preferences.
  3. Under Accessibility, tap Animation & Haptics.
  4. Tap the toggle next to Allow Haptics to enable or disable touch feedback when interacting with buttons in the Slack app.

Who can use this feature?

  • All members
  • Available on all plans

Edit your profile

Help your coworkers learn more about you by completing your profile. As you fill out your profile, don’t forget to upload a profile photo. Your photo makes it easier for your coworkers to know who you are in Slack. People can add the following to their profile:

  • Full name

  • Display name

  • Title

  • Pronouns

  • Name recording

  • Name pronunciation

  • Phone number

  • Time zone

Note: By default, the pronoun field is hidden in Slack profiles. If you don’t see this option, find an owner or admin to ask for help.

Update your profile

Desktop

Mobile

  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Select Profile.
  3. Click Edit.
  4. Edit your profile, then click Save Changes.

Tip: From your profile, click View as to preview how your profile appears to coworkers and external people using Slack Connect.

  1. Tap your profile picture at the top of your screen.
  2. Tap View Profile.
  3. Tap Edit Profile.
  4. Edit your profile, then tap Save.

Note: If your workspace has custom profile fields, keep in mind that it’s not possible to edit them from the Slack mobile apps.

Note: Profile fields with a lock icon can only be edited by an owner or admin. If you need to edit a locked profile field find an owner or admin to ask for help.

Hide a person in Slack

You can hide a person in Slack so that their messages in channels are hidden from you, and you won’t receive notifications when they mention you or send you a direct message (DM).

Screenshot 2023-05-31 at 11.04.35 AM.png

How it works

  • When you hide or unhide someone, they won’t be notified.
  • You can choose to reveal individual hidden messages.
  • A hidden person’s name will only be shown in the header of your DM with them, or if you copy their information from a conversation.

Hide a person

When you hide someone, their profile picture, name and messages will be hidden from you in most places throughout Slack. They’ll be able to join huddles you’re in, but you’ll see a warning letting you know that they’re there, and their name will be hidden.

Desktop

Mobile

  1. Open the profile for the member you’d like to hide.

  2. Click the three dots icon, then choose Hide [Name].

  3. To confirm, click Hide This Person.

  4. Open the profile for the member you’d like to hide.

  5. Tap the three dots icon, then choose Hide [Name].

  6. To confirm, tap Hide This Person.

Note: Hidden members who send you DMs or mention you in channels will not trigger banner notifications, however you’ll still see a badge 1 on the conversation.

View and manage hidden people

Someone you’ve hidden will remain this way until you decide to unhide them.

Desktop

Mobile

  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Select Preferences, then click Privacy & visibility.
  3. Scroll to find the list of People you’ve hidden, then click the x icon to unhide someone.

Tip: You can also unhide someone by opening their profile, clicking the three dots icon, then selecting Unhide.

  1. Open the hidden member’s profile.
  2. Tap the three dots icon.
  3. Tap Unhide [Name].

View a hidden person’s message

When you choose to view a hidden person’s message, their name and photo will remain hidden. To view a message sent by someone you’ve hidden, click or tap Show anyway.

Who can use this feature?

  • All members
  • Available on all plans

Manage animated images and emoji

Some of the custom emoji and GIFs shared in your workspace may move or flash. To manage these animations, you can change your preferences at any time.

Manage animations

Desktop

iOS

Android

  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app

  2. Select Preferences from the menu.

  3. Select Accessibility from the list.

  4. Below Other display options, check or uncheck the box next to Automatically play animations in Slack.

  5. Tap your profile picture at the top of your screen.

  6. Tap Preferences.

  7. Under Accessibility, tap Animation & Haptics.

  8. Tap the toggle next to Allow Animated Images on or off, or tap the toggle next to Sync with iOS to match this setting with your device.

  10. Tap Preferences.

Tip: On your desktop, you can collapse any image by clicking the arrow icon beside the image name.

Manage your channel suggestions

To help you discover other channels to join, you can opt to receive channel suggestions from Slack. Channel suggestions are based on your activity and they’re only visible to you.

Set your channel suggestion preference

  1. From your desktop, click your profile picture. 28 Profile Menu.png
  2. Select Preferences.
  3. Click Advanced.
  4. Under Other Options, check or uncheck the box next to Send me occasional channel suggestions.

Note: Slack may also recommend channels to leave or archive based on how frequently they’re used. You will only see prompts to archive channels you created.

Who can use this feature?

  • Members (but not** guests**)
  • Available on paid plans

Manage your contact sharing preferences

By default, people from your organization and anyone you work with in Slack Connect channels and direct messages (DMs) can share certain contact information from your Slack profile with other people they work with in Slack. In addition to your full name and company name (which are already visible to people you’re connected to), contact information includes your display name, profile picture, email address (depending on your workspace settings). If you’d like, you can adjust this preference so only people from your organization, or no one at all, can share your contact info with the people they work with in Slack.

Note: If you don’t want to connect with someone who has received your contact info, you can ignore their invitation or block future invitations.

Adjust your contact sharing preference

  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Select Preferences.
  3. Click Privacy & visibility in the left-side column.
  4. Below Contact sharing, select an option.

Who can use this feature?

  • By default, all members (but not guests)
  • Available on paid plans

Manage your emoji preferences

In Slack, emoji are both fun and helpful for getting work done. To get the most out of emoji, you can adjust your default skin tone, display preferences, and one-click emoji reactions.

Choose your default skin tone

Desktop

iOS

Android

  1. Click the smiley face icon in the message field to open the menu.
  2. Click the ✋ hand icon in the bottom right corner. Emoji menu showing skin tone selection option
  3. Choose a default skin tone.

Tip: You can click on certain emoji when they appear in the message field to quickly cycle through available skin tones.

  1. Tap your profile picture at the top of your screen.

  2. Tap Preferences.

  3. Under Appearance, tap Default Emoji Skin Tone.

  4. Choose your preferred skin tone.

  5. Tap your profile picture at the top of your screen.

  6. Tap Preferences.

  7. Under Appearance, tap Default emoji skin tone.

  8. Choose your preferred skin tone.

Set your emoji display preferences

There are a few preferences for managing how emoji display in Slack:

  • Display emoji as Unicode or plain text
  • Choose to make emoji larger in messages without text
  • Convert typed emoticons to emoji
  1. From your desktop, click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Select Preferences from the menu.
  3. Select Messages & media.
  4. Under Emoji, check or uncheck the boxes to set your preferences.

Note: Slack displays emoji in Apple’s style on Mac and iOS devices, and Google’s style on Windows, Linux, and Android devices.

Set your preference for one-click emoji reactions

One-click emoji reactions let you respond to messages in Slack almost instantly — simply hover over a message and choose from three emoji options. Owners and admins can choose default one-click reactions you see, but you can customize them using the steps below.

  1. From your desktop, click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Select Preferences.
  3. Select Messages & media.
  4. Under Emoji, check or uncheck the box next to Show one-click reactions on messages. If checked, click the boxes to select three emoji.

Manage your keyboard layout

On your desktop, Slack will automatically detect the layout of your keyboard to make sure the app is in sync. If for some reason Slack can’t detect what keyboard you’re using, you’ll have the option to manually adjust your keyboard preference.

Note: The preference to select your keyboard layout can only be set if Slack can’t detect the keyboard you’re using.

Select your keyboard layout

  1. From your desktop, click your profile picture in the sidebar. 28 Profile Menu.png
  2. Select Preferences.
  3. Select Language & region.
  4. Under Keyboard layout, open the drop-down menu to select an option.

Tip: If you use keyboard shortcuts to navigate Slack, there are a few that may differ depending on the keyboard layout you’ve chosen.

Manage your language preferences

You can display the Slack app in a number of languages. If your preferred language isn’t yet supported, you can still send and read messages in that language by adjusting your spellcheck settings.

Supported languages

  • Chinese (Simplified or Traditional)
  • English (U.S. or U.K.)
  • French (France)
  • German (Germany)
  • Italian
  • Japanese
  • Korean
  • Portuguese (Brazil)
  • Spanish (Latin America or Spain)

Note: Slack does not support right-to-left languages. We hope to include better support for these languages in the future.

Change your language preference

To select your preferred language in Slack, use the steps below. Keep in mind that while your selected language will display throughout Slack, you may see some messages display in your workspace’s default language.

Android

  2. Select Preferences from the menu.

  3. Select Language & region.

  4. Below Language, choose an option from the drop-down menu.

  5. Tap your profile picture at the top of your screen.

  6. Tap Preferences.

  8. Select your preferred language.

  9. Tap your profile picture at the top of your screen.

  10. Tap Preferences.

** Manage spellcheck in Slack**

You can send messages in most languages by typing them in your preferred language in the message field. Spellcheck in Slack is enabled by default, and will automatically detect the language of the messages you send. In the message field, misspelled words will appear underlined in red. To manage spellcheck and adjust your spellcheck languages, use the steps below.

Mac

Windows

Set specific spellcheck languages for macOS

In the Slack desktop app versions 4.5.0 and above, Slack will use the system-level macOS spellchecker. By default, macOS spellcheck is set to Automatic by Language and will spellcheck any supported language you type in. If you choose a set of specific languages to be spellchecked on your device, Slack will only spellcheck those languages.

  1. Open System Preferences.
  2. Select Keyboard.
  3. Click the Text tab at the top.
  4. Below Spelling, open the drop-down menu.
  5. Scroll to the bottom of the list, then click Set Up.
  6. Check or uncheck the box next to any languages you’d like spellchecked.

  2. Select Preferences from the menu.

  3. Select Language & region.

  5. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app

  6. Select Preferences from the menu.

  7. Select Language & region.

  8. Check or uncheck the box next to Enable spellcheck on your messages. If enabled, you can add new spellcheck languages by typing the names of those languages in the text field below Spellcheck.

  9. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app

  10. Select Preferences from the menu.

  11. Select Language & region.

  12. Check or uncheck the box next to Enable spellcheck on your messages. If enabled, you can change your spellcheck language by selecting a new one from the drop-down menu.

Manage your Mark as Read preference

Messages in Slack will be marked as read soon after you open a channel or direct message. If you’d like, you can change this preference and select one of these options:

  • Start where you left off and mark the conversation as read
  • Start at the newest message and mark the conversation as read
  • Start at the newest message but leave the unseen messages unread

Set your Mark as Read preference

  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Select Preferences.
  3. Select Mark as read.
  4. Under When I view a channel, select your preference.

Tip: Learn more about reading messages in Slack.

Manage your time zone preferences

Traveling to a new time zone? When you get to where you’re going, you can update your local time zone in Slack.

Change your time zone

Desktop

iOS

Android

Organize your sidebar with custom sections

If you use Slack on a paid plan, you can organize your channels, direct messages (DMs), and apps into custom sections within your sidebar. Your custom sections are only visible to you and won’t affect what your coworkers see, so set them up however you’d like.

Note: If you’re using the free version of Slack, read about ways to manage what’s in your sidebar or start a free trial to use custom sections.

Create custom sections

Desktop

Mobile

  1. From the Home tab, hover over the Channels section in your sidebar. GIF depicting a cursor opening the custom sections modal in the Slack desktop app.

  2. Click the three dots icon.

  3. Click Channel section.

  4. Enter a name for your custom section, or choose one of the suggestions.

  5. Click the smiley face icon to select an emoji to display next to your section.

  6. Click Create.

  7. Open a channel or DM you’d like to create a new section for.

  8. Tap the channel or member name(s) in the conversation header.

  9. Tap the Star (if you have no existing sections) or Move button (if you have sections).

  10. Tap New Section.

  11. Enter a name for your custom section, or choose one of the suggestions.

  12. Tap the smiley face icon to select an emoji to display next to your section.

  13. Tap Create.

Tip: Share a sidebar section with others to invite them to multiple channels at once.

Organize your conversations

Move a conversation to a section

Desktop

Mobile

  1. Open a channel or DM.

  2. Click the star icon (or the emoji associated with the custom section) at the top of the conversation.

Bulk manage conversations

  7. Click the checkmark icon when you are done making changes.

Set your out of office status

When you have to step away from work (like for a vacation or personal leave), you can set an out of office status to let your coworkers know how to get work done or who to contact while you’re gone.

How it works

  • When you set an out of office status, add a message with additional information and set an expiration date to let people know when you’ll be back.
  • Other members will see an ⛔ out of office emoji anywhere they can see your full or display name, and they can view your full out of office status either in your profile or when they hover over your status emoji on desktop.
  • If someone mentions you in a channel, they’ll receive a private message with your out of office status details — like the Slack version of an out of office auto-reply. Your out of office status will also appear above the message field in direct messages (DMs).
  • If you use the Google Calendar or Outlook Calendar apps in Slack, you can automatically sync your out of office status in Slack with those apps.

Note: Members of external organizations can see your out of office status if permitted by your Enterprise organization settings, but your out of office message will only be visible to members of your organization.

Update your out of office status

Set your out of office status
  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Click the Update your status field.
  3. Choose ⛔ Out of office from the list.
  4. Open the drop-down menu below Remove status after… to choose when your out of office status will clear. If you’d like, check the box next to Pause notifications to turn off notifications until your status clears.
  5. If you’d like, add an Out of office message to display on your profile or when someone mentions you in a channel.
  6. Click Save.
Edit or remove your status
  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Select your current status to edit it, or click Clear status to remove it.

Sync with Google Calendar or Outlook Calendar

You can sync your Google or Outlook calendar to automatically set an out of office Status in Slack. When an out of office event in your calendar starts, the default ⛔ out of office emoji will display in your Slack status.

Tip: Schedule your Slack out of office status in advance by adding a future out office event to your calendar.

Manage calendar syncing
  1. From your desktop, click Tools in the sidebar.
  2. Click Apps in the top left.
  3. Search for and select Google Calendar or Outlook Calendar to open the app.
  4. From the app’s Home tab, select Settings.
  5. Click the button to turn out of office syncing on or off.

Who can use this feature?

  • All members
  • Available on Enterprise plans

Set your search preferences

There are two preferences you can set to customize your search options in Slack, depending on whether you’re using the desktop app or Slack in your browser.

Exclude certain channels

From either the desktop app or Slack in your browser, you can exclude certain channels from search results. This preference comes in handy for channels that primarily include automated messages from apps, bots, or workflows.

  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Select Preferences.
  3. Choose Advanced.
  4. Below Search options, add any channels you’d like to exclude from your search results.

Set your keyboard shortcut preference

In many browsers, pressing CmdF (Mac) or CtrlF (Windows/Linux) starts a search in the tab or window you have open. If you use Slack in your browser, you can set this shortcut to open Slack search instead using the steps below.

  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Select Preferences.
  3. Choose Advanced.
  4. Below Search options, check the box next to Cmd F or Ctrl F starts a Slack search.

Set your Slack status and availability

As you work in Slack, it’s helpful to let your team know how quickly you can respond to messages and when you’re available. Slack has a couple of ways to share your whereabouts and indicate your availability to other members.

  • A status isa message that lets others know what you’re up to.
  • Availability refers to thedot next your display name that indicates if you’re active in Slack.

Tip: If you’re a Workspace Owner or Admin, learn how to customize the status suggestions members can choose from.

Update your Slack status

When you set a status in Slack, you’ll see your status emoji appear next to your name. Other members can see your status emoji anywhere they can see your full or display name, and they can view your full status either in your profile or when they hover over your status emoji on desktop. If you don’t select a status emoji, a 💬 speech balloon will display by default.

Desktop

Mobile

Set your status
  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Click the Update your status field.
  3. Enter a status and select an emoji, or choose a suggested status option.
  4. Click Remove status after… to choose when your status will clear. If you’d like, check the box next to Pause notifications to turn off notifications until your status clears.
  5. Click Save.
Edit or clear your status
  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Click your current status to edit it, or click Clear status to remove it.
Set your status
  1. Tap your profile picture.
  2. Tap the status field.
  3. Enter a status, then tap the emoji icon to select an emoji, if you’d like. Or select a suggested status option.
  4. Tap Clear after to choose when your status will clear.
  5. Tap Done.
Edit or clear your status
  1. Tap your profile picture.
  2. Tap your current status to edit it, or tap Clear to clear it.

Note: Depending on your workspace or Grid org settings, your status may be visible to members of other organizations in channels shared externally.

Manage automatic statuses

Slack can let people know that you may be slow to respond based on your activity if you’re in a huddle, in focus mode, or it’s after your working hours.

  1. From your desktop, click your profile picture in the sidebar. A cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Select Preferences.
  3. Under Automatic statuses, check or uncheck the box next to the statuses you want to be updated automatically.

Schedule a status

You can schedule a status in advance when you’ll be away from Slack or otherwise busy, like when you’re on vacation, having lunch, or in an important meeting. Scheduled statuses turn on automatically at the time you set.

Set a scheduled status
  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Click the Update your status field.
  3. Enter a status and select an emoji, or choose a suggested status option.
  4. From the Duration drop-down menu, click Choose a start and end time.
  5. Select a start and end date for your status.
  6. Click Save.
Manage a scheduled status

You can view, edit, or cancel a status before it starts.

  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app
  2. Under Scheduled, click the status you want to manage.
  3. Edit the details and click Save.
  4. To remove a scheduled status, hover over it and click the delete icon.

Tip: You can schedule up to five statuses at a time.

Manage your availability

From the dot next to your name, your coworkers can see whether you’re set to active or away and if you’ve paused your notifications.

Slack automatically determines your availability: you’re set to active when Slack is open on your desktop or mobile device. You’re set to away after 10 minutes of desktop inactivity, or if you navigate away or close the app on your mobile device.

Active ****Erica Fleming as active in Slack****

Away ****Erica Fleming as away in Slack****

Set your availability

If you’d like, you can manually set yourself to active or away at any time.

Desktop

Mobile

  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app

  2. Click Set yourself as away or Set yourself as active.

  3. Tap your profile picture.

  4. Tap Set yourself away or Set yourself as active.

Upload a profile photo

Your profile photo helps your team know who you are in Slack. And if your photo is clear, it’ll be easier for someone to pick you out in a crowd or a meeting!

Add a profile photo

Desktop

iOS

Android

  2. Select Profile from the menu.

Remove a profile photo

You can remove your profile photo from Slack on the desktop app or browser, but it’s not currently possible to do this from our mobile apps.

  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar. Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app

Use dark mode in Slack

Dark mode helps make working in Slack easier on your eyes by using a darker, higher-contrast color theme. You can turn on dark mode from your Slack preferences, or sync dark mode in Slack with your operating system (OS) settings on certain devices.

Adjust your dark mode preference

Desktop

iOS

Android

  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar.

    Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app

  2. Select Preferences from the menu, then select Appearance.

  3. Under Color Mode, select Dark.

  4. Click the close icon when you’re done.

  5. Tap your profile picture at the top of your screen.

  6. Tap Preferences.

  7. Under Appearance, select Color Mode.

  8. Select an option: Always Light, Always Dark, or Follow System Settings.

  9. Tap your profile picture at the top of the screen.

  10. Tap Preferences.

  11. Select Dark Mode.

  12. Choose your Dark Mode preference: System default, Off, or On.

Note: The dark mode preference is device specific, so setting it on the desktop app won’t apply to the mobile app.

Sync dark mode with your OS settings

You can sync dark mode in Slack with your operating system settings. This is supported on Mac, Windows, iOS 13 and above, and Android 10 and above.

Desktop

iOS

Android

  1. Click your profile picture in the sidebar.

    Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app

  2. Select Preferences from the menu, then select Appearance.

  3. Under Color Mode, select System.

  5. Tap Preferences.

  6. Under Appearance, select Color Mode.

Channels

Accept a Slack Connect channel invitation

Slack Connect makes it possible to work alongside people from other companies in the same Slack channel. If you’ve been invited to join another organization’s channel, learn how to accept an invite.

Note: Owners and admins can restrict who can accept invitations. If you’re unable to accept one, find an owner or admin and ask for help.

View and accept an invitation

If multiple people from your organization have received an invitation for the same channel, only one person needs to accept it. If your workspace isn’t using a paid Slack plan, you may see the option to upgrade your workspace or start a free trial.

Desktop

iOS

Android

  1. From Home, click Directories

  2. Click External.

  3. Review the invitation details to see who invited you and any other organizations that may also be working in the channel. When you’re ready, click Accept.

  4. Review the channel settings, then click Accept and Join Channel.

  5. Tap your profile picture at the top of your screen.

  6. Tap Invitations to connect.

  7. Review the invitation details. If the sender included a message, tap View message to read it. When you’re ready, tap Accept.

  8. Choose the workspace you’d like the channel to be a part of, then review the channel settings. Tap Confirm to finish.

  9. Tap your profile picture at the top of your screen.

  10. Tap Slack Connect invitations.

  11. Review the invitation details. If the sender included a message, tap View message to read it. When you’re ready, tap Accept.

  12. Choose the workspace you’d like the channel to be a part of, then review the channel settings. Tap Confirm to finish.

Note: If you don’t see Directories, look for the External connections tab in the sidebar instead. You may need to click More to find it.

Note: Your admins may need to approve Slack Connect channel invitations you accept.

Who can use this feature?

  • By default, all members (but not guests)
  • Available on paid plans

Add a channel to multiple workspaces in your Enterprise organization

In an Enterprise organization, Org Owners, Org Admins, and members with permission can add channels to multiple workspaces. A multi-workspace channel allows people across an organization, like those in different departments, to work together in the same channel from their separate workspaces.

Tip: Multi-workspace channels can be org-wide, meaning they’re added to every workspace in your org, and set as default channels for members.

Create a multi-workspace channel

Any channel (except for the #general channel) can be added to multiple workspaces in your org.

  1. From your desktop, open an existing channel or create a new one.
  2. Click the channel name in the conversation header.
  3. Next to Workspaces with access to this channel, click Edit.
  4. Search for and select workspaces you’d like to have access this channel.
  5. Click Save.

Note: Some apps and custom bots may not be available in a multi-workspace channel.

Remove a multi-workspace channel from a workspace

  1. From your desktop, open the multi-workspace channel you’d like to update.
  2. Click the channel name in the conversation header.
  3. Next to Workspaces with access to this channel, click Edit.
  4. Click next to workspaces you’d like to remove the channel from.
  5. Click Save.

Note: Org Owners or Org Admins with permission can add or remove a channel from workspaces using channel management tools.

Who can use this feature?

  • Org Owners, Org Admins, and members with permission
  • Available on Enterprise plans

Add people to a channel

Slack organizes conversations into dedicated spaces called channels. Add people to channels to bring the right people and information in your workspace together in one place (for people outside your company, learn how to use Slack Connect to invite them to a channel).

GIF showing a cursor adding people to a channel in Slack

Add people to a channel

You can add up to 1,000 people to a channel at once. For large groups, we recommend copying a list of full names or email addresses from another channel in Slack or another service before following the steps below. If email addresses are hidden in member profiles, you won’t be able to add people to channels using email addresses.

Tip: To help onboard new members, owners and admins can set default channels for them to automatically join.

Desktop

Mobile

  1. Open the channel you’d like to add people to.

  2. Click the member icon in the top right.

  3. Click Add people.

  4. To add a few people, search for the members you’d like to add by name, email address, or user group (if you’re using a paid plan) and select them. To add a large group, paste the list of names or email addresses into the field.

  5. When you’re done, click Add.

  6. Open the channel you’d like to add people to.

  7. Tap the channel name at the top.

  8. Tap Add.

  9. To add a few people, search for the members you’d like to add by name or email address and select them. To add a large group, paste the list of names or email addresses into the field.

  10. When you’re done, tap Add.

Tip: On paid plans, you can invite a usergroup to a channel on mobile with the /invite @[usergroup] slash command.

Note: On the Business+ and Enterprise plans, owners and admins with permission can add people to channels with channel management tools.

Who can use this feature?

  • All members and Multi-Channel Guests
  • Available on all plans

Archive or delete a channel

When a channel is no longer needed, it can be archived or deleted (except for the the #general channel or #all-companyname channel). Archived channels are closed to new activity, but the message history is retained and searchable on paid plans. Deleted channels are permanently removed from a workspace, message history included.

Note: If you can’t archive or delete a channel, find a Workspace Owner or Admin to ask for help.

Archive a channel

By default, all members (except guests) can archive channels they’re a member of, but Workspace Owners and Org Owners can restrict this permission to certain role types. Channel managers can always archive channels they’re assigned to.

Archive a channel

Desktop

Mobile

  1. Open the channel you’d like to archive.

  2. Click the channel name in the conversation header. Gif of a cursor clicking the channel name in the channel header

  3. Click Settings, then Archive channel for everyone.

  4. Click Archive channel to confirm.

  5. If you set up your channel with a template, the canvases and lists will remain accessible in Slack, while the workflows will be unpublished. To delete a canvas, list, or workflow added as part of a template, check the box next to its name, then click Delete.

  6. Open the channel you’d like to archive.

  7. Tap the channel name in the conversation header.

  8. Tap Archive channel. Scroll down if you don’t see the option.

  9. Tap Archive to confirm.

Tip: On the Business+ and Enterprise plans, people with permission to use channel management tools, can also archive and delete channels from a central dashboard.

Unarchive a channel

If you change your mind, you can unarchive a channel. If the channel is private, the channel members will be retained, but if it’s public, the former members will not be restored.

  1. From ** Home, click Directories**.
  2. Click the Channels tab.
  3. Search for the channel by name or description, or click the Channel type filter and select Archived channels.
  4. Select the channel you’d like to unarchive from the list.
  5. Click the channel name in the conversation header.
  6. Click Settings, then click Unarchive this channel.

Note: If you don’t see Directories, look for the Channels tab in the sidebar instead. You may need to click More to find it.

Tip: Channel names can’t be repeated. To reuse the name of an archived channel, you’ll need to unarchive it and rename the channel.

Delete a channel

On the Free, Pro, and Business+ plans, only Workspace Owners and Workspace Admins can delete channels. In an Enterprise organization, Org Owners can restrict channel deletion to certain role types or assign channel deletion to a custom role.

Note: Deleting a channel is permanent, so make sure to proceed with care.

Delete an active channel
  1. From your desktop, open the channel you’d like to delete.
  2. Click the channel name in the conversation header. Gif of a cursor clicking the channel name in the channel header
  3. Click Settings, then Delete channel.
  4. Select Delete this channel.
  5. Check the box next to Yes, permanently delete the channel, then click Delete Channel.
Delete an archived channel
  1. From ** Home, click on Directories**.
  2. Click the Channels tab.
  3. Search for the channel by name or description, or click the Channel type filter and select Archived channels.
  4. Select the channel you’d like to delete from the list.
  5. Click the channel name in the conversation header.
  6. Click Settings, then Delete this channel.
  7. Check the box next to Yes, permanently delete the channel, then click Delete Channel.

Note: Retention settings do not apply to messages in deleted channels. If you delete a channel, any messages sent in the channel will be permanently deleted as well.

Convert a channel to private or public

When you create a channel, you can choose to make it either public or private. Public channels are best for sharing information that anyone can find and read, while private channels are meant for discussions that shouldn’t be open to everyone. If you need to change this setting later, you can convert a channel to private or public.

Keep in mind

  • Files shared in a channel that is converted to public will also become public. Once made public, files will remain public even if the channel is converted back to private.
  • Slack Connect channels can’t be converted to public if they’re private in the organization that owns the channel. Otherwise, when you convert a Slack Connect channel, it will only be converted for the organization that made the change.
  • The #general or #all-company channel can’t be converted to private.

Note: On the Business+ and Enterprise plans, owners and admins can convert channels to private with channel management tools.

Convert a channel

When you convert a channel, a message will post in the channel to let members know it’s been converted.

Convert to private

Convert to public

  1. From your desktop, open the channel you’d like to make private.
  2. Click the channel name in the conversation header. Gif of a cursor clicking the channel name in the channel header
  3. Select the Settings tab.
  4. Scroll down and click Change to a private channel.
  5. Click Change to Private to confirm.

By default, owners, admins, and Channel Managers can convert a channel to private, but owners can restrict this. If you can’t convert a channel to private, find an owner and ask for help.

  1. From your desktop, open the channel you’d like to make public.
  2. Click the channel name in the conversation header. Gif of a cursor clicking the channel name in the channel header
  3. Select the Settings tab.
  4. Scroll down and click Change to a public channel.
  5. Click Change to Public to confirm.

By default, Workspace Owners, Org Owners, and Org Admins can convert private channels to public, but owners can restrict this. If you can’t convert a channel to public, find an owner and ask for help.

Who can use this feature?

  • Workspace Owners/Admins,** Org** Owners/Admins, and Channel Managers can convert a channel to private Workspace Owners and Org Owners/Admins can convert a channel to public
  • Available on all plans

Copy member names and email addresses from a conversation

Copy member information from a conversation

Create a channel

Channels are the best way to keep conversations organized in Slack. You can create a channel for just about any project, topic, or team and whatever else you can think of!

GIF of a cursor clicking the plus icon in the Slack desktop app

Create a channel

Desktop

Mobile

  1. Click the plus sign in the sidebar.

  2. Select Channel. If you’re on a paid plan, you can select Blank channel to set up a regular channel, or choose a template to automatically set your channel up for a specific purpose (like managing a project, handling approvals, and more).

  3. Enter a channel name and choose whether your channel should be public or private, then click Create.

  4. From the Home tab, tap the plus sign.

Create and share custom channel templates

Slack channel templates bundle canvases, lists, and workflows together in a channel. If you can’t find a template that suits your needs, you can mix and match any number of canvases, lists, and workflows to create a template customized for your organization and how you get work done.

** What to expect**

  • You can add as many canvases, lists, and workflows to your template as you’d like.
  • When adding canvases and lists, you can choose from those you’ve created, or existing templates. There are seven pre-configured workflows you can use to send messages to channels and collect information via forms.
  • Anyone with permission to create custom templates can share the link with others to use. On Enterprise plans, owners, admins, and Template Admins can also publish custom templates to the the template gallery for members to use.

** Create a template**

By default, all members can create and share custom templates. If you don’t see this option, find an owner or admin to ask for help.

Get started
  1. From your desktop, click ** Tools** in the sidebar.
  2. Click ** Channel Templates**.
  3. Click Build a Template in the top right corner.

Note: If you don’t see the Tools tab in your sidebar, look for the Automations tab instead. You may need to click More to find it.

** Add components**
  1. Below What’s included, click ** Add to template. Then, select Canvas, List, or Workflow**.
  2. To add a canvas or a list, search for the one you want to use, or select one from the list. Then, click Add to template.
  3. To add a workflow, select one from the list and click Add to template. The workflows available for templates are pre-configured and cannot be customized further.
** Finish up**
  1. When you’re done adding components to your template, click Finish Up.
  2. Give your template a name, and add a description.
  3. Add a channel prefix. Prefixes help standardize channel names so it’s easy for people to find channels for projects, processes, etc.
  4. If you’d like, you can give others access to edit your template by adding them as a template manager. Below Who can edit this template?, search for people you’d like to add and select their names.
  5. If you’re on Enterprise Grid, certain people may have permission to publish custom templates to the template gallery for other members of their org to use. To publish your template to the gallery, select Members of [org name] below Who can find and use this template.
  6. Click Save Template. You can access your custom template from the ** Your templates** section of the gallery.

** Share a template**

You can share links to templates with other people in your workspace or Enterprise Grid org. Anyone with a link to your template can use it when creating a new channel, or add it to an existing channel.

  1. From your desktop, click ** Tools** in the sidebar.
  2. Click ** Channel Templates, then select Your templates**.
  3. Click the ** three dots icon** next to a template, then select Copy template link from the menu.
  4. Share the link in any channel or direct message (DM).

Tip: For more details on using templates, visit Work with templates in channels.

** Edit a template**

To modify a template you created or that you manage, follow the steps below:

  1. From your desktop, click ** Tools** in the sidebar.
  2. Click ** Channel Templates, then select Your templates**.
  3. Click the ** three dots icon** next to a template.
  4. To make changes to the canvases, lists, or workflows in the template, select Edit this template. To update the template name, or add or remove template managers, click Edit template name and permissions. Then, click Save Changes.
  5. To delete the template, select Delete template, then click Delete Template to confirm.

Who can use this feature?

  • All members (by default)
  • Available on paid plans

Guide to Slack channel templates

Slack templates bundle canvases, lists, and workflows together in a channel to get any job done. Instead of creating a channel to manage a process from scratch, choose a template and fill in key details.

Creating a new Slack channel using the project starter kit template

How templates work

  • You can create a new channel from a template, or add a template to an existing channel. After selecting a template, the canvases, lists, and workflows it includes will be created for you, so anyone can access them from dedicated tabs in the channel header.
  • Once your template is set up, you can fill in details and customize it further if you’d like. For example, you might need to add your own documents to the canvas, or change the list so it shows information in a specific order.
  • If canvases or lists are disabled for your workspace or Enterprise organization, or you don’t have access to Workflow Builder, you will not be able to use templates.

Tip: Create a custom template so your teammates can set up channels that match your company’s unique way of working. Anyone can create custom templates and share them with other members of their workspace or Enterprise org.

Browse templates

  1. From your desktop, click More in the sidebar.
  2. Select Templates to open the template gallery.
  3. Browse templates by topic or department (like Project Management or Marketing) if you’d like, or scroll to view all available templates.
  4. Click on a template to see an interactive preview.

Template spotlight

Here are more details on a few of the templates we offer:

Project starter kit

New hire onboarding

Feedback intake

Project starter kit template preview

Everything you need to kick off a new project. This template includes:

Project overview canvas for sharing project briefs, meeting notes, etc.

Task tracker list to organize tasks and deliverables

Workflow that posts automatically when tasks are updated

New hire onboarding template preview

Simplify the process of bringing new people up to speed with a dedicated onboarding channel and resources. This template includes:

Onboarding guide canvas to centralize company resources and required documents

First week to-do list to organize and track tasks

Workflow that automatically adds your new hire to all channels you specify

Feedback intake.png

Streamline and prioritize feedback submissions from your team, customers, or partners. This template includes:

Feedback instructions canvas to share submission guidelines

Feedback tracker list to group and prioritize submissions

** Workflows** to collect feedback submissions and post automatically when submissions are updated

Get started

Pick a template from the gallery, or follow the steps below:

  1. From your desktop, click the plus button in the sidebar.
  2. Select Channel.
  3. Below Try a template, choose the template you’d like to use, then click Next.
  4. Slack will automatically add a channel prefix relevant to the template. Enter the rest of the channel name, and choose a workspace from the drop-down menu if you’re on an Enterprise plan. Then, click Next.
  5. Choose a channel type (public or private), then click Create.
  6. You can invite people to your channel now, but we recommend waiting to add people until you’ve finished setting up your template.
  7. When it’s ready, Slack will post a message to the channel letting you know. To access the newly-created canvas, list, and workflows that are part of your template, click the corresponding tab in the channel header.
  8. Some information will be pre-filled in the canvas (like section headings) and list (for example, placeholder tasks you can edit or remove). Workflows included in templates don’t require additional configuration, but you can edit them if you’d like.

Note: For a step-by-step guide to using and customizing templates, visit Work with templates in channels.

FAQs

I don’t have access to some of the features included in templates. Can I still use them?

In order to use templates, canvases and lists have to be enabled for your workspace or org, and you need permission to create workflows with Workflow Builder. If you can’t access one or more of these features, you won’t see the option to create channels with templates or add templates to existing channels.

Can I hide certain templates from the gallery?

Not right now. Members of your workspace or org with access to templates will be able to view and use templates created by Slack and by other members.

Can I add more than one template to a channel?

Yes, you can. If you no longer need the canvas, lists, and workflows from a template, you can remove them from the channel, or archive it.

How do I create and share my own templates with others?

By default, anyone can create a custom template for other members of their workspace or org to use. Owners and admins can restrict who has permission to create custom templates, and they can also edit and delete custom templates. On Enterprise plans, owners and admins can also manage who has permission to publish custom templates to the template gallery.

What happens to canvases, lists, and workflows created as part of a template if I archive or delete the channel?

When you archive or delete a channel with a template, the canvases and lists will remain available, and the workflows will be unpublished. You’ll be prompted to delete them as part of the archive or deletion flow, but you can skip this step if you don’t want to remove them from Slack entirely.

Who can use this feature?

  • All members (by default)
  • Available on paid plans

Join a channel

Slack organizes conversations in your workspace into dedicated spaces called channels. Channels bring the right people, tools, and information together for a common purpose — like working on a specific project, or discussing a particular topic with your team. Keep reading to learn how to find and join channels in your workspace.

Tip: If you’ve been invited to work with another company in a channel using Slack Connect, learn how to accept the invitation.

Join channels

All members (but not guests) can browse and join public channels in their workspace. To join a private channel, you must be added by an existing member of the channel.

Desktop

Mobile

  1. From Home, click Directories.

  2. Click the Channels tab.

  3. Browse the list of public channels in your workspace, or search for a channel by its name or description.

  4. Select a channel from the list to view it.

  5. Click Join Channel.

  6. Tap the search bar at the top of your screen.

  7. Tap Channels.

  8. Browse the list of public channels in your workspace, or search for a channel by its name.

  9. Tap a channel name to open it, then tap Join Channel.

Temporarily join a channel

You can temporarily join a public channel. They’ll appear in the Temporary channels section in the sidebar, and you’ll automatically be removed after your set period of time.

  1. From desktop, visit a channel you want to join temporarily.
  2. Click the arrow on the Join Channel button.
  3. Choose how long you want to be in the channel: Just for today, For 48 hours, or For 1 week.

Who can use this feature?

  • All members except** guests**
  • Available on all plans

Leave a channel

In Slack, work happens in channels — organized spaces for everything related to a project, topic, or team. If a channel is no longer relevant, you can leave it at any time. Here are a few things to keep in mind:

  • No one can leave the general channel.
  • Single-Channel Guests can’t leave the channel they have access to.
  • Multi-Channel Guests can leave private channels, but must be removed from public channels by an owner or admin. To rejoin any channel, they must be added back.

Note: If you leave a private channel, its messages and files will no longer appear in your search results. To rejoin, you’ll need to be added back by another member of that channel.

Leave channels

Desktop

Mobile

  1. Open the channel you’d like to leave. GIF displaying a cursor clicking on a channel header in the Slack app to open the channel details modal.
  2. Click the channel name in the conversation header.
  3. Click Leave channel.

Tip: To leave multiple inactive channels at once, open the Manage my sidebar menu from the Home tab and click Leave inactive channels.

  1. Open the channel you’d like to leave.
  2. Tap the channel name in the conversation header.
  3. Tap Leave Channel.

Who can use this feature?

  • All members
  • Available on all plans

Let additional organizations join a Slack Connect channel

If you have an existing Slack Connect channel with another organization, someone from the invited organization must allow additional organizations to join the channel.

Tip: To see which organization owns a channel, click the channel name and scroll to the Organizations section of the About tab.

Let additional organizations join a channel

  1. From your desktop, open the channel you’d like to let additional organizations join.
  2. Click the channel name in the conversation header. 14_Leave_channel_GIF.gif
  3. Click the Settings tab.
  4. Under Organizations, click Add people.
  5. Check the box next to Let additional organizations join this channel.
  6. Click Done.

For the organization that owns the channel, people with permission to manage Slack Connect channels will be notified that additional organizations can now join the channel.

Who can use this feature?

  • Workspace Owners/Admins and members with permission (Pro and Business+ plans), Org Owners/Admins and members with permission (Enterprise plans)
  • Available on paid plans

Remove organizations from a Slack Connect channel

When a project comes to an end, you may no longer need to work with another organization in a Slack Connect channel. You can remove your organization from another company’s channel, or remove organizations from your company’s channel.

What to expect

  • The company that owns the channel can continue using it. Organizations with permission to post, invite, and more can see an archived copy of the channel if their organization is removed. Organizations with permission only to post will not get an archived copy.
  • Files added by members from other organizations will no longer be accessible.
  • As long as you remain connected in at least one other channel, people from your organizations can continue to send direct messages (DMs). Otherwise, they can invite each other to communicate in DMs.

Tip: To end all communication in Slack with an organization you’ve been working with, learn how to disconnect.

Remove organizations from a channel

From your desktop, open the channel you’d like to remove your organization or other organizations from. If your company owns the channel, repeat the steps above for each organization you’d like to remove.

  1. From your desktop, open the channel you’d like to remove your organization or other organizations from.
  2. Click the channel name in the conversation header. Gif of a cursor clicking the channel name in the channel header
  3. Click the Settings tab.
  4. Under Organizations, hover over the organization you’d like to remove and click the three dots icon.
  5. Click Remove, then Remove Organization to confirm.

Note: On the Business+ and Enterprise plans, owners and admins can disconnect individual external people instead of removing entire external organizations.

Who can use this feature?

  • Workspace Owners/Admins and members with permission (Pro and Business+ plans), Org Owners/Admins and members with permission (Enterprise plans)
  • Available on paid plans

Remove someone from a channel

Slack organizes conversations into dedicated spaces called channels. When someone no longer needs to be a part of a channel, they can be removed. By default, Workspace Owners and Admins can remove people from public channels, and members can remove people from private channels.

What to expect

  • Anyone can be removed from a channel by those with permission.
  • All members and guests need to be added back to a private channel to rejoin it, and guests also need to be added back to a public channel to rejoin it.
  • It’s not possible to remove people from the #general or #all-companyname channel.

Note: Workspace Owners and Org Owners can restrict who has permission to remove people from channels. If you’re unable to remove someone from a channel, find an owner and ask for help.

Remove people from channels

When you remove someone from a channel, Slack will notify that person.

Workspace Owners and Admins can rename any public channel (including the general channel) and private channels they’ve joined. Members can rename any channel they manage.

Note: On the Business+ and Enterprise plans, owners and admins with permission can rename public and private channels with channel management tools.

Slack Connect guide: Work with external organizations

Rather than using email to communicate, you can use Slack Connect to work alongside people from external organizations in a Slack channel or direct message (DM). Read on for an overview of Slack Connect.

Slack Connect for channels

When you need to work as a group, you can use a Slack channel to host up to 250 organizations. Here’s what to keep in mind:

  • To work in channels together, each organization must be using a paid Slack plan.
  • Like other channels in Slack, people can join the channel or be added to it by someone else from their organization.
  • People from different organizations working together in channels can send each other DMs. To work in a group DM, everyone in the conversation must be in at least one channel together.

Tip: If you’d like to work with an organization that’s either not using Slack nor on a paid Slack plan, you can invite them to try Slack Connect for free.

Channel ownership

Your organization owns any channels created in your workspace or Enterprise organization. When using Slack Connect, only the organization that owns a channel can do the following:

  • Invite organizations
  • Remove other organizations
  • Manage posting permissions
  • Continue using the channel if external organizations have been removed or disconnected
Using apps and workflows

When using apps and workflows in a channel with people outside your company, here’s what to expect:

  • You can decide who can use workflows, but some workflows can never be used in Slack Connect.
  • Shortcuts associated with apps are available to people from other organizations if an app is installed to their workspace. When people take an action from an app shortcut, it will only apply to the account they’ve connected to the app.
  • Apps added by another organization will include that organization’s Slack icon next to the app name. Only people from the organization that added an app can remove it from a channel.
  • People in the channel can see messages from bots and apps. They can also exchange messages with an app’s bot user if it’s been added to the channel.
  • Your organization’s custom apps and shortcuts can only be used by your organization, but messages posted by the app or shortcut can be seen by everyone in the channel.

Slack Connect for DMs

If you’d like to communicate one-on-one with someone from an external organization, you can use a DM. On any Slack plan, you can start a DM by sending someone an invitation, or accepting an invitation you’ve received.

Using Slack Connect

Here’s what to expect when working with external people in Slack channels and DMs.

Security

Slack Connect provides a secure way for organizations to communicate and collaborate together. Read more about how data management features apply to Slack Connect and Slack’s enterprise-grade security.

Identify Slack Connect conversations

When you hover over a channel name or DM, you’ll see if any external organizations are in the conversation. You’ll also see a banner with the same information when you view the conversation. By default, all your Slack Connect channels and DMs will be organized into the External Connections section in your sidebar.

Manage Slack Connect

To manage Slack Connect all in once place, from Home click Directories, then select External. You’ll find the option to send and accept invitations, manage your invitations, and more.

View member profiles

Organizations can choose what profile information other organizations can see: either just basic details, like names and profile photos, or additional details like statuses and timezones. Profile photos for external people will be marked with their organization’s Slack icon in the bottom-right corner.

Using custom emoji

You can use your organization’s custom emoji like you would in any other channel or DM. External people can see your organization’s custom emoji and add them to their organization so that they can use the same emoji too.

Learn more: For an in-depth look at Slack Connect, take our course and test your knowledge to earn a Slack Skills badge.

Slack Connect: Disconnect from an organization

You can disconnect from an organization to end all communication with them in Slack Connect channels and direct messages (DMs).

Note: Disconnecting from an organization affects all channels they’re a part of (even channels owned by another organization) and can’t be undone.

What to expect

Depending on the permissions in your Slack Connect channels, here’s what to expect when you disconnect from an organization:

  • Invited organizations with permission to post, invite and more will retain an archived read-only copy of the channel (but note that he channel can’t be unarchived). Those with permission only to post will not retain a copy.
  • The disconnected channel will remain usable by the channel owner.
  • DMs will be archived for all participants, with all message history intact.
  • Member profile details such as profile photos and display names will continue to update in disconnected conversations.
  • Files shared in channels and DMs by people from other organizations will no longer be accessible.

Note: Instead of disconnecting, you can remove other organizations from Slack Connect channels if you’d like.

Disconnect from an organization

Pro and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

By default, only Workspace Owners and Admins can disconnect from organizations, but they can allow all members to take this action by granting them permission to approve and manage Slack Connect channels.

  1. From your desktop, click your workspace name in the sidebar.
  2. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Workspace Settings. (If you manage more than one workspace, choose one from the drop-down menu.)
  3. Below Administration in the left sidebar, select Slack Connect connections. If you don’t see the left sidebar, click Menu in the top-left corner to find it.
  4. Next to the organization you’d like to disconnect from, click the three dots icon.
  5. Select Disconnect [organization name], then click Disconnect.

Org Owners and Admins can disconnect from an organization:

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Organization settings.
  3. Click Slack Connect in the left sidebar, then Connections.
  4. Next to the organization you’d like to disconnect from, click the three dots icon.
  5. Select Disconnect [organization name], then click Disconnect.

Note: You can also disconnect from an organization automatically using the Slack Connect API.

Who can use this feature?

  • Workspace Owners/Admins and Org Owners/Admins
  • Available on paid plans

Use Salesforce channels in Slack

Salesforce channels are a type of Slack channel that correspond to Salesforce records, like Accounts or Opportunities. Salesforce channels let your team centralize conversations about customers, drive deal progress, and update Salesforce records, all in Slack.

Note: Owners and admins must configure Salesforce channels in order for members to use them. If you’re not able to use Salesforce channels in Slack, reach out to an owner or admin and ask for help.

GIF demonstrating Salesforce channels in Slack How it works

  • Salesforce channel names are based on fields from their corresponding records, which means they can include spaces, capital letters, and other characters that are not allowed in standard Slack channels.
  • When you create or join a Salesforce channel, it’ll be added to your sidebar in a Salesforce channels section (but you can move it to another custom section if you’d like).
  • Your permissions in Salesforce channels match your permissions for the corresponding record. If you have permission to access the record in Salesforce, you can access the corresponding Salesforce channel; if you have permission to edit the record in Salesforce, you can edit the record in Slack.

Note: It’s not possible to invite external people to Salesforce channels.

Components of a Salesforce channel

The features of your Salesforce channels are organized into tabs. These are the tabs you can expect to see in a Salesforce channel and what they can help you do.

Messages Use the messages tab for conversations related to the corresponding record like updating your teammates on an important deal or discussing a new Opportunity. Just like a typical Slack channel, these conversations can include discussions with channel members, messages from apps, and more.

Record details The record details tab uses data from Salesforce to give you a snapshot of the record the channel is mapped to. From the record details tab, you can learn key details about the record and its related accounts and update it right in Slack. The name of the record details tab will match the type of record the Salesforce channel is associated with. For example, a Salesforce channel associated with an Account will have an Account details tab.

Summary (available on the Business+ and Enterprise+ plans) Use the summary tab to get up to speed quickly with an AI-generated summary of conversations in all of the Salesforce channels associated with the corresponding record. Click the More details icon next to a summary to review its sources and jump to the conversation in Slack.

Related conversations Find other relevant conversations connected by Salesforce record relationship in the related conversations tab. When you select the related conversations tab, you’ll see other channels that are automatically associated with the Salesforce channel based on record relationships, but you can also click Add to manually add a channel to the list of related channels.

Related records If your admins choose a record type for the Default list tab when configuring Salesforce channels, that record type will display in the related records tab. If you have permission to update the record type, any changes you make in Slack will be reflected in Salesforce.

Note: Any channel member can participate in the Messages tab, but access to Salesforce data is based on a user’s permissions to view and edit Salesforce records.

Create a Salesforce channel

You can create a new Salesforce channel from any record that appears in Slack. On the Enterprise Grid plan, only people who can create org-wide multi-workspace channels can convert a channel to a Salesforce channel.

Desktop

Mobile

  1. From a record in Slack, click Create Channel in the top-right corner.

  2. Choose to Create a new channel or Link an existing channel, then follow the prompts to finish.

  3. From a record in Slack, tap Create Channel.

  4. Tap Create Channel or Link Existing channel then follow the prompts to finish

Note: If a Salesforce channel has already been created for a record’s parent record, you’ll be prompted to use that channel (but you can still create a new one if you’d like).

Update a record from a Salesforce channel

To save time switching between Slack and Salesforce, you can update a record right from the channel. You can edit a record in Slack if you have permission to edit it in Salesforce. It’s not possible to edit rich text and geolocation Salesforce fields in Slack.

Desktop

Mobile

  1. Open the Salesforce channel for the record you’d like to update.

  2. Select the Record details tab.

  3. Under Record details, update any fields you have permission to edit.

  4. Open the Salesforce channel for the record you’d like to update.

  5. Tap the conversation header then select Opportunity details.

  6. Next to Record details tap Edit, then update any fields you have permission to edit.

Note: On Business+ and Enterprise plans, use list views to share customized collections of records and update Salesforce data in Slack.

Automate Salesforce channel invitations

On the Business+ and Enterprise Grid plans, use Workflow Builder to automatically add relevant stakeholders to a Salesforce channel when an event is triggered in Salesforce. For example, you can set up a workflow to create a Salesforce channel and add the Opportunity Owner and Sales Manager when the opportunity amount decreases by 10%.

  1. From your desktop, click Tools in the sidebar.
  2. From Workflows, click New in the top right.
  3. Select Build Workflow.
  4. Below Start the workflow, click Choose an event, then select Start with a Salesforce event.
  5. Set up your workflow trigger, then click Continue.
  6. Click Add steps, then select Salesforce channels.
  7. Choose Create Salesforce channel or Find Salesforce channel from record ID, then configure the step.
  8. Below Suggested step, select Add people to a channel, then configure the step.
  9. Complete your workflow, then select Finish up.

Note: If you don’t see ** Tools, look for Automations** in the sidebar instead. You may need to click ** More**.

Use Salesforce channels in Salesforce

If configured by your Salesforce System Admins, you can also access a Salesforce channel from its corresponding record directly in Salesforce. Any messages and updates will sync instantly across both Slack and Salesforce, so you can communicate with your team where it’s most convenient for you.

What you can do

Here are the actions you can take from Salesforce channels in Salesforce:

  • Send and format messages
  • Reply in threads
  • Upload files
  • Add emojis and use emoji reactions
  • Mention people
  • Invite people to channels

Note: The Slack experience in Salesforce is limited. More complex actions such huddles, clips, and workflows can only be completed in Slack. For more information, visit the Salesforce Help Center.

Who can use this feature?

  • All members
  • Available on all plans
