  5. Next to AI agent experience or AI assistant experience, click Edit.
  6. Select Enabled or Disabled, then click Save.

Assistants and agents will display in all workspaces where the app is installed.

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Organization settings.
  3. Click ** Integrations** in the left sidebar and select Installed apps.
  4. Search for an app or choose one from the list.
  5. From the app page, click App Settings.
  6. Next to AI agent experience or AI assistant experience, click Edit.
  7. Select Enabled or Disabled, then click Save.

Tip: Members can also interact with agents and assistants from an app’s Home tab.

Who can use this feature?

  • Workspace Owners/Admins and Org Owners/Admins
  • Available on paid plans

Manage access to AI features in Slack

Slack offers a variety of AI features that allow people in your workspace or Enterprise organization to quickly summarize conversations, take notes during huddles, and more. Owners and admins can manage access to AI features to restrict usage or turn certain features off entirely.

Feature availability

The AI features available to you in Slack depend on your plan:

  • Pro – Business+ – Enterprise+
  • Member feedback on AI responses* – ✓ – ✓ – ✓
  • Suggested sidebar sections – ✓ – ✓ – ✓
  • Conversation summaries – ✓ – ✓ – ✓
  • Huddle notes – ✓ – ✓ – ✓
  • Automatic search filters – ✓ – ✓ – ✓
  • Search answers – ✓ – ✓
  • Recaps – ✓ – ✓
  • File summaries – ✓ – ✓
  • Translations – ✓ – ✓
  • Workflow automation – ✓ – ✓
  • AI workflow steps – ✓ – ✓
  • Message explanations – ✓ – ✓
  • Canvas content generation – ✓ – ✓
  • Slackbot – ✓ – ✓
  • Enterprise search – ✓

*Members’ ability to submit feedback to Slack on AI responses is blocked in some workspaces or Enterprise organizations by default. Owners and admins in these workspaces or orgs can override this setting to allow feedback submissions.

Manage AI feature access

Pro, Business+, and Enterprise Select

Enterprise Grid and Enterprise+

  1. From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar.

  2. Select Workspace settings from the menu, then click ** Roles & permissions**.

  3. Click Feature access and select AI.

  4. Next to the AI feature you’d like to manage, click Edit and choose whether Everyone or No one can use it. Some AI features include other settings you can manage in addition to deciding who can use them.

  5. Click Save.

  6. From the Home tab, click your organization name in the sidebar.

  7. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Organization settings.

  8. Click Roles & permissions and select Feature access.

  9. Click AI.

  10. Next to the AI feature you’d like to manage, click Edit and choose who can use it — No one, Only specific people and groups, Everyone except specific people and groups, or Everyone. Some AI features include other settings you can manage in addition to deciding who can use them.

  11. Select any groups you’d like, then click Next to select individual users.

  12. Click Save.

Manage additional settings

There are additional settings available for some AI features:

  • Feature – Settings
  • Huddle notes –
    • Whether people can change the automatic huddle notes setting in channels
  • Search –
    • Whether people can share responses
    • Whether files can be used to generate responses
  • AI workflow steps –
    • Whether files can be included in AI steps
    • Whether third-party connectors can be used in AI steps
  • Message explanations –
    • Whether people can share responses
  • Slackbot –
    • Whether Slackbot can create and edit canvases
    • Whether files can be used to generate responses
    • Whether Slackbot can search the web

Note: The additional file setting you choose for search answers will also apply to Slackbot responses (or vice versa).

Who can use this feature?

  • Workspace Owners/Admins and Org Owners/Admins
  • Available on paid plans

Manage canvas settings in Slack

Canvases are surfaces built into Slack where members can create and share fully-formatted content. Channel and direct message (DM) canvases are available on all plans, while standalone canvases are only available on paid plans. Owners and admins can manage access to canvas version history, and turn off canvas update messages for channel and DM canvases.

Manage canvas version history

Anyone with permission to edit a canvas can access its revision history and restore a previous version. If you’d like, you can disable canvas version history so that only the most recent version is available.

Free, Pro, and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

  1. From your desktop, click ** Admin** in the sidebar.
  2. Select Workspace settings from the menu.
  3. Next to Canvases, click Expand.
  4. Check or uncheck Show canvas version history and allow restoration.
  5. Click Save.

Org Owners and Admins can manage canvas version history for everyone in your org.

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Hover over Tools & settings, then select Organization Settings.
  3. Click Settings in the left sidebar, then select Organization Settings.
  4. Next to Canvases, click Edit.
  5. Check or uncheck Show canvas version history and allow restoration.
  6. Click Save.

Manage canvas sharing settings

By default, anyone with permission to edit a canvas can grant others access to view or edit it, but you can restrict this so that only the canvas owner can grant access to others. If you don’t restrict this, members of your workspace or Enterprise organization can choose whether they’d like to restrict sharing on canvases they create.

Free, Pro, and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

  1. From your desktop, click ** Admin** in the sidebar.
  2. Select Workspace settings from the menu.
  3. Next to Canvas sharing, click Expand.
  4. Check or uncheck Limit sharing so only canvas owners can share their canvases with other people and channels.
  5. Click Save.

Org Owners and Admins can manage canvas sharing for everyone in your organization. It isn’t possible to manage canvas sharing at the workspace level.

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Hover over Tools & settings, then select Organization Settings.
  3. Click Settings in the left sidebar, then select Organization Settings.
  4. Next to Canvas sharing, click Edit.
  5. Check or uncheck Only allow canvas owners to share canvases with other people and channels.
  6. Click Save.

Manage canvas update messages

When someone in your workspace or organization updates a channel or DM canvas, or a canvas in a tab, we’ll send a message to the conversation to help keep other members informed of the changes. You can turn these update messages off, or allow members to manage canvas update messages in individual conversations.

Free, Pro, and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

  1. From your desktop, click ** Admin** in the sidebar.
  2. Select Workspace settings from the menu.
  3. Next to Canvas update messages, click Expand.
  4. Check or uncheck Disable canvas update messages.
  5. Click Save.

Org Owners and Admins can turn canvas update messages off for their organization, or allow Workspace Owners and Admins to manage update messages for their workspace(s).

Org level
  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Hover over Tools & settings, then select Organization Settings.
  3. Click Settings in the left sidebar, then select Organization Settings.
  4. Next to Canvas update messages, click Edit.
  5. Check or uncheck Disable canvas update messages.
  6. Select Org-wide channels or All channels to decide where update messages should be disabled.
  7. Click Save.
Workspace level

If canvas update messages are turned on at the org level, you can manage them for individual workspaces. Disabling canvas update messages will turn them off only for the channels in that workspace.

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Hover over Tools & settings, then select Organization Settings.
  3. Click Settings in the left sidebar, then select Workspace Settings.
  4. Select a workspace from the drop-down menu, then click Open.
  5. Next to Canvas update messages, click Expand.
  6. Check or uncheck Disable canvas update messages.
  7. Click Save.

Manage canvas printing

By default, members of your workspace or Enterprise organization can print canvases they have access to, but you can disable this if you’d like.

Free, Pro, and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

  1. From your desktop, click ** Admin** in the sidebar.
  2. Select Workspace settings from the menu.
  3. Next to Canvas printing, click Expand.
  4. Check or uncheck Anyone with view or edit access to a canvas can print it.
  5. Click Save.

Org Owners and Admins can manage canvas print settings for everyone in your org.

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Hover over Tools & settings, then select Organization Settings.
  3. Click Settings in the left sidebar, then select Organization Settings.
  4. Next to Canvas printing, click Edit.
  5. Check or uncheck Anyone with view or edit access to a canvas can print it.
  6. Click Save.

Who can use this feature?

  • Org Owners/Admins (Enterprise plans) and Workspace Owners/Admins (Pro and Business+ plans)
  • Available on all plans

Manage channel posting permissions

You can adjust who’s allowed to post to channels or use mentions that notify all channel members. This helps keep large channels, like those used for announcements, on topic and free from distraction.

Note: Owners can restrict who can set posting permissions. If you don’t see this option, find an owner and ask for help.

Manage who can post in channels

Free and Pro plans

Business+ and Enterprise plans

You can change who can post messages in the #general channel. This channel will be read-only for anyone without permission to post.

  1. From your desktop, open the #general channel.
  2. Click the channel name in the conversation header. 14_Leave_channel_GIF.gif
  3. Select the Settings tab.
  4. Next to** Posting permissions, click Edit**.
  5. Select who can post and reply to messages. If you’re specifying specific people, you can select up to 100.
  6. Click Save Changes.

You can change who can post in any channel. A channel will be read-only for anyone without permission to post.

  1. From your desktop, open the channel you’d like to adjust posting permissions for.
  2. Click the channel name in the conversation header.
  3. Select the Settings tab.
  4. Next to** Posting permissions, click Edit**.
  5. Select who can post and reply to messages. If you’re specifying specific people, you can select up to 100 per channel.
  6. Click Save Changes.

Tip: On the Business+ and Enterprise plans, owners and admins with permission can manage channel posting permissions with channel management tools.

Manage who can notify a channel

Free and Pro plans

Business+ and Enterprise plans

You can change who can use @everyone to notify all members of the #general channel.

  1. From your desktop, open the #general channel.
  2. Click the channel name in the conversation header.
  3. Select the Settings tab.
  4. Next to** Posting permissions, click Edit**.
  5. Check or uncheck the box next to Allow @everyone mentions.
  6. Click Save Changes.

You can change who can use @everyone to notify all members of the #general channel. You can also change who can use @here or @channel to notify members in other channels.

  1. From your desktop, open the channel you’d like to adjust posting permissions for.
  2. Click the channel name in the conversation header.
  3. Select the Settings tab.
  4. Next to** Posting permissions, click Edit**.
  5. Check or uncheck the box next to Allow @here and @channel mentions. (For the #general channel, you’ll see Allow @everyone mentions.)
  6. Click Save Changes.

Who can use this feature?

  • All members (default)
  • Available on all plans

Manage custom canvas template settings

Custom canvas templates can be shared in your workspace or Enterprise organization to standardize long-form content in Slack. Owners and admins can manage which members in their workspace or org can create and share custom canvas templates. In an Enterprise org, Org Owners and Admins can also manage permissions for publishing custom templates to the canvas template gallery.

Choose who can create canvas templates

Everyone (except guests) can create and share canvas templates, but you can restrict this permission to certain roles if you’d like.

Pro and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

  1. From your desktop, click ** Admin** in the sidebar.

  2. Select Workspace settings from the menu, then click ** Roles & permissions**.

  3. From the Account types page, click the** three dots icon** next to Create canvas templates for a team.

  4. Click Edit permission.

  5. Choose which roles can create canvas templates.

  6. Click Save.

  7. From the ** Home** tab, click your organization name in the sidebar.

  8. Hover over Tools & settings, then click Organization settings.

  9. Click ** Roles & permissions, then select Account types**.

  10. Click the three dots icon next to Create canvas templates for a team, then select Edit permission.

  11. Choose which roles can create canvas templates.

  12. Click Save.

Choose who can publish templates to the template gallery

By default, Org Owners and Admins and Workspace Owners and Admins in an Enterprise org can publish canvas templates to the Created by your organization section of the template gallery. To restrict this to Org Owners and Admins, follow the steps below:

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Hover over Tools & settings, then click Organization settings.
  3. Click ** Roles & permissions, then select Account types**.
  4. Click the three dots icon next to Publish canvas templates for the organization, then select Edit permission.
  5. Choose which roles can publish org-wide canvas templates.
  6. Click Save.

Assign Template Admins

By default, only owners and admins in an Enterprise org can publish canvas templates to the Created by your organization section of the template gallery. To allow other members to do this, you can assign them the Template Admin system role.

Note: An owner, admin, or Template Admin will also need to have Can edit access to the template to unpublish it from the gallery.

Who can use this feature?

  • Workspace Owners/Admins (Pro and Business+) and Org Owners/Admins (Enterprise plans)
  • Available on paid plans

Manage custom emoji permissions

By default, any member (but not guests) can create custom emoji. If they’d like, Workspace Owners and Org Owners can choose which role types can create and delete custom emoji.

Change custom emoji permissions

Free, Pro, and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

Org level

Manage email display

By default, members’ email addresses are displayed in their Slack profiles, which are visible to their organization and any external organizations they work with in Slack Connect. If they’d like, owners and admins can adjust this setting to display email addresses only to members of their organization, or to no one at all.

Display or hide email addresses

When email addresses are displayed in Slack profiles, members can use them to search for people they work with. If email addresses are hidden, they still may be accessible through apps, test tokens, or the API.

Free, Pro, and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

  1. From your desktop, click ** Admin** in the sidebar.

Org level

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.

Who can use this feature?

Set your workspace signup mode

Manage join and leave messages

In Slack, messages are shown when someone joins, is added to, or leaves a channel to let other members know who’s coming and going. Workspace Owners and Workspace Admins on Free, Pro, and Business+ plans can manage these messages and choose to turn them off if they’d like.

Message in a channel showing that four new people have joined

Manage join and leave messages

By default, messages are shown when someone joins, is added to, or leaves a channel. Smaller groups might find these messages helpful, but larger groups might prefer to hide them. If you’re a Workspace Owner or Workspace Admin, use the steps below to manage join and leave messages for your workspace.

  1. From your desktop, click ** Admin** in the sidebar.
  2. Select Workspace settings from the menu.
  3. Scroll down to the Channel Join & Leave Messages section and click Expand.
  4. Check or uncheck the box next to Show a message when people join or leave channels.
  5. Click Save.

If join and leave messages are turned off

👀 Messages are displayed…

  • When someone joins or is added to a public or private channel
  • If someone leaves a private channel

🙈 Messages aren’t displayed…

  • When someone joins or is added to a public channel with more than 20 members
  • If someone leaves a public channel
  • If someone’s account is deactivated

Who can use this feature?

  • Workspace Owners and** Workspace Admins**
  • Free, Pro, and Business+ plans

Manage link previews

When someone shares a link in Slack, others can see a text preview of the content. Owners and admins can adjust preview settings for websites and third-party apps.

Turn off previews for specific websites

Workspace Owners and Admins can turn off link previews for specific websites.

  1. Hover over a link shared in the desktop app.
  2. Click the close icon in the top left to remove the preview.
  3. Check the box next to Also block previews from this website in the future and select an option from the drop-down menu.
  4. Click Remove and Block to confirm.
Manage blocked previews
  1. From the Home tab, click your workspace name in the sidebar.
  2. Hover over Tools & settings, then select Workspace settings.
  3. Click the Attachments tab.
  4. Under Blocked previews, review the list of websites with previews turned off. Click the x icon to remove a website from the list and turn previews back on.

Note: In Enterprise organizations, link previews for websites are managed at the workspace level.

Manage work object previews

Pro and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

Org Owners and Org Admins can manage work object previews.

  1. From the Home tab, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Hover over Tools & settings, then click Organization settings.
  3. From the left sidebar, click Settings then select Organization settings.
  4. Click Edit next to Work object previews.
  5. Select a preview setting, then click Save.

Pro and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

  2. Click Manage apps.

Org Owners and Admins can manage work object previews for specific apps.

Manage list settings in Slack

Members in your workspace or Enterprise organization can use Slack lists to track projects and manage tasks. Owners and admins can disable lists and limit sharing permissions to list owners only.

Enable or disable lists

Free, Pro and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

  2. Select Workspace settings from the menu.

  3. Next to Lists, click Expand.

  4. Select Enable or Disable, then click Save.

  5. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.

  6. Hover over Tools & settings, then click Organization settings.

  7. From the left sidebar, click Settings, then select Organization settings.

  8. Next to Lists, click Enable or Disable.

Manage list sharing settings

By default, everyone with edit access to a list can grant others view or edit access. You can limit this so that for all lists in your workspace or organization, only the list owner can grant access to others. If you don’t adjust this setting, members of your workspace or organization can choose whether to limit sharing on lists they create.

Free, Pro and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

  1. From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar.

  2. Select Workspace settings from the menu.

  3. Next to List Sharing, click Expand.

  4. Check or uncheck Limit sharing so only list owners can share their lists with other people and channels, then click Save.

  5. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.

  6. Hover over Tools & settings, then click Organization settings.

  7. From the left sidebar, click Settings, then select Organization settings.

  8. Next to Lists, click Edit.

  9. Check or uncheck Only allow list owners to share lists with other people and channels.

  10. Click Save.

Who can use this feature?

Manage permissions for message editing and deletion

By default, all members can edit and delete their own messages, but it is possible to change these permissions. Here’s what can be adjusted:

  • Owners and admins can choose when to allow message editing.
  • Owners can choose who can delete their own messages.

Tip: Restricting the ability to edit or delete messages may impact how members communicate. Consider the pros and cons of editing and deleting for your team’s needs.

Choose when to allow message editing

Free, Pro, and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

Workspace Owners and Admins can choose when to allow message editing: any time, never, or up to a certain timeframe.

  1. From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar.
  2. Select Workspace settings from the menu.
  3. Click the Permissions tab.
  4. Next to Message Editing, click Expand.
  5. Use the drop-down menu to choose when members can edit messages.
  6. Click Save.
Org level

Org Owners and Org Admins can choose when to allow message editing: any time, never, or up to a certain timeframe. This policy will apply to every workspace in the org.

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Organization settings.
  3. Click Settings in the left sidebar, then select Organization Policies.
  4. Click the Permissions tab.
  5. Next to Message Editing, click Add Policy or Edit.
  6. Choose when members can edit messages, then click Save Policy.
Workspace level

If an org policy hasn’t been set, Workspace Owners and Workspace Admins can choose when to allow message editing: any time, never, or up to a certain timeframe.

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Workspace settings. If you manage more than one workspace, choose one from the drop-down menu.
  3. Click the Permissions tab.
  4. Next to Message Editing, click Expand.
  5. Use the drop-down menu to choose when members can edit messages.
  6. Click Save.

Note: If you select Never, this change will immediately take effect and members will no longer be able to edit their messages.

Choose who can delete their messages

Free, Pro, and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

Workspace Owners can choose which role types can delete their messages. This permission will also affect who can unsend messages.

  1. From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar.
  2. Select Workspace settings from the menu.
  3. Select Roles & Permissions in the left sidebar.
  4. Click the three dots icon next to Delete own messages, then select Edit permission.
  5. Check or uncheck the boxes to choose who can delete messages, then select Save.
Org level

Org Owners can choose which role types can delete their own messages (this permission will also affect who can unsend messages). They can also decide whether to apply this policy to the entire organization or to allow individual workspaces to edit this permission.

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Organization settings.
  3. Click Roles & permissions in the left sidebar, then select Account types.
  4. Click the three dots icon next to Delete own messages, then select Edit permission.
  5. Check or uncheck the boxes to decide who can delete their messages. You can also decide whether individual workspaces can edit this permission.
  6. Select Save.
Workspace level

If Org Owners allow, Workspace Owners can decide for their workspace which role types can delete their messages. This permission will also affect who can unsend messages.

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Workspace settings. If you manage more than one workspace, choose one from the drop-down menu.
  3. Select Roles & permissions in the left sidebar.
  4. Click the three dots icon next to Delete own messages, then select Edit permission.
  5. Next to Message Editing & Deletion, click Expand.
  6. Check or uncheck the boxes to choose who can delete messages, then select Save.

Who can use this feature?

  • Workspace Owners/Admins and Org Owners/Admins

Manage Sales Home in Slack

Sales Home in Slack is a surface where members with the Slack Sales Home User permission set can update Salesforce objects, set up and receive notifications for important deals, and more. Once you’ve set up your Salesforce connection, you can manage Sales Home settings for your workspace or Enterprise organization.

Note: Workspace Primary Owners (Business+) and members with the Roles Admin system role (Enterprise plans) can assign the Sales Admin system role to members.

Add Salesforce orgs

Once you’ve connected Salesforce and Slack, you can add orgs to Sales Home:

  1. From your desktop, click Sales in the sidebar. If you don’t see Sales, click More to find it.
  2. Click the gear icon.
  3. Click the Salesforce org drop-down menu and select Add Salesforce org.
  4. Select Add a new Salesforce org, then click Connect.

Slack will automatically connect to Salesforce and begin syncing your data. This normally takes a few minutes, but can take longer for orgs with more data.

Note: Admins in Salesforce can manage member access to Sales Home by assigning the Slack Sales Home User permission set.

Set up Salesforce object lists

Sales teams can use Salesforce lists to easily update Salesforce objects in Slack. Users can see list views for any object they have access to in Salesforce. You can also suggest up to 25 default lists per object to surface specific lists to your team when they update Salesforce objects in Slack.

  1. From your desktop, click Sales in the sidebar. If you don’t see Sales, click More to find it.
  2. Click the gear icon.
  3. Click ** Salesforce lists**.
  4. Click ** Add object**.
  5. Select a Salesforce object. If you’d like, suggest default lists for the object.
  6. Click Save.

Note: To remove a Salesforce object, click the three dots icon next to it, then click Remove object.

Create and manage Sales Home notifications

Create custom notifications

Sales Admins can create notifications in Sales Home to help their teams stay informed about new opportunities, important deals, and more.

  1. From your desktop, click Sales in the sidebar. If you don’t see Sales, click More to find it.
  2. Click the gear icon.
  3. Select Notifications.
  4. Next to Admin-created notifications, click Manage.
  5. Click Create notification.
  6. Choose a template, then select from the options to customize it.
  7. Click Save notification.
Manage custom notifications

Sales Admins can edit or delete any admin-created notifications.

  1. From your desktop, click Sales in the sidebar. If you don’t see Sales, click More icon to find it.
  2. Click the gear icon.
  3. Select Notifications.
  4. Next to Admin-created notifications, click Manage.
  5. Click the three dots icon next to a notification.
  6. Select Edit or Delete, then click Save notification or Delete notification to confirm.

Tip: You can view more details about the notifications created by your organization in the Notifications section of the Sales settings dashboard.

Configure notification settings

You can control where Sales Home notifications are sent by restricting them to specific channel types or workspaces (in an Enterprise organization).

Channel settings

Workspace settings

  1. From your desktop, click Sales in the sidebar. If you don’t see Sales, click More to find it.

  2. Click the gear icon.

  3. Select Notifications.

  4. Next to Channel restrictions, click Edit.

  5. Select a channel type.

  6. Check or uncheck the box next to Include Slack Connect external channels.

  7. Click Save.

  8. From your desktop, click Sales in the sidebar. If you don’t see Sales, choose the More icon to find it.

  9. Click the gear icon.

  10. Select Notifications.

  11. Next to Workspace restrictions, click Edit.

  12. Select the workspace(s) you’d like to enable notifications for.

  13. Click Save.

Note: Configure a Slack Record Layout in Salesforce to customize the fields and notifications members can edit in Slack.

Manage deal celebrations

Deal celebrations on member profiles help recognize personal achievements and foster team excitement. Deal celebration banners will appear on member profiles for three days after a deal is won and can be shared to any conversation in Slack to spread the word.

  1. From your desktop, click Sales in the sidebar. If you don’t see Sales, click More to find it.
  2. Click the gear icon.
  3. Select Celebrations.
  4. Click the toggle next to Show deal won celebration.
  5. Customize what will be shown on the celebration, then click Save.

Tip: If you use custom stage fields, you can choose a custom stage for “win”.

Who can use this feature?

  • Sales Admins
  • Available on the new version of Business+and Enterprise+ plans
  • Available on the Business+ and Enterprise Grid plans with the legacy Slack Sales Elevate add-on

Manage Slack Connect channel invitation settings and permissions

Slack Connect allows members of your organization to work with people from external organizations in the same channel. Keep reading to learn more about the types of invitations your organization can send and the permissions they grant to external people working in your channels.

Invitation types and permissions

You can decide what type of invitation your members can send when they’d like to collaborate with external people in your organization’s channels. There are two invitation types you can manage: Permission only to post and Permission to post, invite, and more. The invitation types determine what permissions external people will have in the channels they’re invited to.

Note: Once the invitation has been accepted, anyone with permission to send Slack Connect invitations can adjust the existing permissions for the external people.

Permissions by invitation type

  • Permission only to post – Permission to post, invite, and more

  • Send messages – ✓ – ✓

    Use emoji and reactions

    – ✓ – ✓

    Add files

    – ✓ – ✓

    Use workflows

    – ✓ – ✓

    Edit the channel layout

    – ✓ – ✓

    Use their team’s shortcuts

    – ✓ – ✓

    Add other people from organizations already in the channel

    – ✓

    Add apps and workflows

    – ✓

    Change a channel name, topic, or description*

    – ✓ – ✓

    Convert a channel to public or private*

    – ✓

    Add a channel to multiple workspaces in their Enterprise org

    – ✓ – ✓

  • See an archived copy of a channel if their organization is removed – ✓

  • Set a retention policy* – ✓

*Note: These changes will only apply to the workspace where they were made, and not for other organizations in the channel.

  5. Check or uncheck the box next to Allow Slackbot to create and edit canvases or Include files in search results. If you include files, choose whether Slackbot can access all shared files or only uploaded files.

  6. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.

  7. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Organization settings.

  8. Click Roles & permissions and select Feature access.

  9. Click AI.

  10. Next to Slackbot, click Edit.

  11. Check or uncheck the box next to Allow Slackbot to create and edit canvases or Include files in search results. If you include files, choose whether Slackbot can access all shared files or only uploaded files.

  12. Click Save.

Manage web search

By default, Slackbot cannot search the web when generating responses. Owners and admins can allow web search, and choose whether to warn users before they open links cited in Slackbot responses.

Business+ and Enterprise Select plans

Enterprise Grid and Enterprise+ plans

  1. From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar.

  2. Select Workspace settings from the menu.

  3. Below Settings, click Slackbot.

  4. Next to Web search, click Expand.

  5. Check the box next to Allow Slackbot to surface content from web domains in search to turn web search on.

  6. If you’d like, check the box next to Warn users before opening web results to display a warning each time someone clicks on a link to view it outside of Slack.

  7. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.

  8. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Organization settings.

  9. Click Settings, then click Slackbot.

  10. Next to Web search, click Edit.

  11. Check the box next to Allow Slackbot to surface content from web domains in search to turn web search on.

  12. If you’d like, check the box next to Warn users before opening web results to display a warning each time someone clicks on a link to view it outside of Slack.

Note: Web search may send your data outside of the FedRAMP authorization boundary.

Who can use this feature?

  • Workspace Owners/Admins and Org Owners/Admins
  • Available on the new version of Business+and Enterprise+ plans
  • Available on the legacy Business+, Enterprise Select, and Enterprise Grid plans with the Slack AI add-on

Manage Slackbot access to connected Salesforce organizations

Slackbot can find information from any Salesforce orgs connected to your Slack workspace or Enterprise organization. By default, Slackbot can create or update records. Owners and admins can restrict access to certain orgs if they’d like, and decide which Salesforce record actions Slackbot can take.

Note: When generating a response that includes Salesforce data, Slackbot will only include information available to people based on their permissions in Salesforce.

Manage Slackbot access

Business+ and Enterprise Select plans

Enterprise Grid and Enterprise+ plans

  1. From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar.

  2. Select Manage Salesforce organizations from the menu.

  3. Select a Salesforce org.

  4. Click the Settings tab.

  5. Click the toggle next to Allow Slackbot to access data from this organization.

  6. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.

  7. Hover over Tools & settings, then click Manage Salesforce organizations.

  8. Select a Salesforce org.

  9. Click the Settings tab.

  10. Click the toggle next to Allow Slackbot to access data from this organization.

Choose whether Slackbot can manage records

If Slackbot has access to a Salesforce org, you can restrict Slackbot’s ability to take certain Salesforce actions or block it from taking record actions entirely. When your members ask Slackbot to take Salesforce actions, they’ll always be prompted to review and approve before any changes are made.

Business+ and Enterprise Select plans

Enterprise Grid and Enterprise+ plans

  1. From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar.

  2. Select Manage Salesforce organizations from the menu.

  3. Select a Salesforce org.

  4. Click the Settings tab.

  5. Next to Allow Slackbot to create and update records, click Edit.

  6. Click Allowed in the drop-down menu, then select Allow only for some objects, Allow for all objects except excluded ones, or Not allowed.

  7. Click Save.

  8. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.

  9. Hover over Tools & settings, then click Manage Salesforce organizations.

  10. Select a Salesforce org.

  11. Click the Settings tab.

  12. Next to Allow Slackbot to create and update records, click Edit.

  13. Click Allowed in the drop-down menu, then select Allow only for some objects, Allow for all objects except excluded ones, or Not allowed.

  14. Click Save.

Who can use this feature?

  • Org Owners/Admins (Enterprise plans) and Workspace Owners/Admins (Business+ plans)
  • Available on the new version of Business+ and Enterprise+ plans
  • Available on the legacy Business+ and Enterprise Grid plans with the Slack AI add-on

Manage Slackbot skills

Skills give Slackbot step-by-step instructions for handling specific tasks so you get the right output every time. Owners and admins can decide who can automatically make certain skills available for groups of people and publish skills to the skill catalog for members to find and customize.

What to expect

  • Members can browse and add available skills from the Skills tab in Slackbot. Once someone adds a skill to their Skills tab, Slackbot can use it when generating responses.
  • Workspace and Org Owners can assign the Skill Manager system role from the admin dashboard.
  • Skill Managers can assign skills to groups, publish skills to the catalog, and view skill usage data from the Slackbot Skills tab.

Note: Any member can create and share skills, but only Skill Managers can add skills to the catalog and assign them to others.

Assign Skill Managers

By default, Workspace Owners/Admins and Org Owners/Admins can manage skills. To grant others permission, Workspace Owners (on Business+ and Enterprise Select) and Roles Admins (on Enterprise Grid or Enterprise+) can assign the Skill Manager system role.

Business+ and Enterprise Select plans

Enterprise Grid and Enterprise+ plans

  1. From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar.
  2. Select Workspace settings from the menu, then click Roles & permissions.
  3. Click Roles.
  4. Click the three dots icon next to Skill Manager and select Assign people.
  5. Select people, then click Assign.

The Organization Primary Owner and org-level Roles Admins can assign the Skill Manager role.

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Hover over Tools & settings, then click Organization settings.
  3. Click Roles & permissions, then select Roles.
  4. Click the three dots icon next to Skill Manager and select Assign people.
  5. Select people, then click Save.

Note: Members aren’t notified when they’re assigned a system role.

Manage skills

Skill Managers can assign skills to specific groups of people and add skills to the catalog for members to browse.

Assign skills to groups

When you assign a skill to a group of people, Slackbot will know to use that skill when responding to relevant prompts. Any updates you make to skills you’ve assigned apply immediately, so Slackbot will always use the latest version.

  1. From your desktop, open Slackbot.
  2. Click the Skills tab.
  3. Click Manage skills.
  4. Next to a skill, click the three dots icon.
  5. Select Auto-enable for user groups.
  6. Click Specific user groups, then click Next.
  7. Choose user groups and click Save. All members of the user group will see the skill in their Slackbot Skills tab.
Add skills to the catalog

Add a skill to the catalog for members to find and use. Anyone can add a skill from the catalog to use as-is, or make a copy to customize a skill however they’d like.

  1. From your desktop, open Slackbot.
  2. Click the Skills tab.
  3. Click Manage skills.
  4. Next to a skill, click the three dots icon.
  5. Select Publish to skill catalog.

View skill usage data

Skill Managers can also view usage data for skills. Here’s what’s available:

  • Skill name
  • Skill creator
  • Groups assigned the skill
  • Whether it’s published to the skill catalog
  • How many times it’s been used
  • How many people have used it

To view usage data, follow the steps below:

  1. From your desktop, open Slackbot.
  2. Click the Skills tab.
  3. Select Manage skills.
  4. Click on a skill to view the usage data.

Who can use this feature?

  • Workspace Owners/Admins, Org Owners/Admins, and Skill Managers
  • Available on the new version of Business+ and Enterprise+ plans
  • Available on the Business+, Enterprise Select, and Enterprise Grid plans with the legacy Slack AI add-on

Manage third-party calling app settings

In addition to Slack huddles, you can choose a third-party calling app as an additional calling option for your workspace or Enterprise organization. When you enable a third-party calling app, members can start a call from the headphones icon.

Note: Slack permits phone calls, but only via a third-party provider and app. You will need to contract for internet or telecommunications service from them directly. Slack does not charge you for using these integrations.

Select third-party calling apps

Keep in mind that choosing a third-party app may require you and your members to create an account with that service.

Pro and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

  2. Select Workspace settings from the menu.
  3. Next to Third-party call providers, click Expand.
  4. Below Calling options, check the box next to your preferred app.
  5. Click Save.

On the Pro and Business+ plans, Workspace Owners and Admins can select multiple third-party calling apps for members to choose from.

Manage user groups from the admin dashboard

User groups are a great way to communicate with multiple members at once and to easily assign members to roles, permissions, and channels.

At a workspace level, owners and admins can allow other members to create, disable, or modify user groups, as well as create @admin and @owner user groups to easily notify all of the admins and owners in a workspace or organization.

In an Enterprise organization with multiple workspaces, Org Admins and Owners can create and manage org-level groups to provision members across multiple workspaces.

Set user group permissions

Pro and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

  1. From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar.
  2. Select Workspace settings from the menu, then click Roles & permissions.
  3. From the Account types page, click the three dots icon next to Create and edit user groups.
  4. Click Edit permission, then choose who can create and edit user groups and click Save.
Org level

Org Owners and Org Admins can set an org policy to manage user group permissions for every workspace in their org.

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Organization settings.
  3. Click Roles & permissions in the left sidebar.
  4. From the Account types page, click the three dots icon next to Create and edit user groups.
  5. Click Edit permission, then choose who can create and edit user groups, and and click Save.
Workspace level

If an org policy hasn’t been set, Workspace Owners and Admins can set user group permissions for workspaces they manage.

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Hover over Tools & settings, then click Workspace settings. (If you manage more than one workspace, choose one from the drop-down menu.)
  3. Click Roles & permissions in the left sidebar.
  4. From the Account types page, click the three dots icon next to Create and edit user groups.
  5. Click Edit permission, then choose who can take the action and click Save.

Manage org-level user groups

Owners and admins in Enterprise organizations can create org-level groups from the admin dashboard and use them to assign roles, permissions, and workspace membership. These groups can only be managed in the dashboard and can’t be combined with IDP groups.

Edit org-level user groups

Edit org-level user groups to manage group details (like the group’s name or description), membership, or visibility (whether the group is mentionable in Slack).

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Hover over Tools & settings, then click Organization settings.
  3. Click People in the left sidebar, then click Groups.
  4. Click the three dots icon next to the group you want to manage.
  5. In the menu, choose whether you want to Edit group details like group name or description, Add members, Remove members, or Edit group visibility.
  6. Make your changes, then click Save.
Manage workspace membership
  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Hover over Tools & settings, then click Organization settings.
  3. Click People in the left sidebar, then click Groups.
  4. Click the three dots icon next to the group you want to manage.
  5. Click Connect workspaces, then check or uncheck the box next to the workspaces you want the group to be joined to.
  6. Click Next, then select which workspaces you want to have mandatory membership.
  7. Click Assign Workspaces.
Manage channel membership
  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Hover over Tools & settings, then click Organization settings.
  3. Click People, then click Groups.
  4. Click the three dots icon next to the group you want to manage.
  5. For user groups connected to at least one workspace, you’ll have the option to click Connect channels. If you don’t see this option, add the group to a workspace.
  6. Check or uncheck the box next to the channels you want the group to join.
  7. Click Add channels.

Tip: Use the search bar in the top right of the selection screen to filter the list of channels.

Who can use this feature?

Slack Connect allows members of your organization to work with people from external organizations in the same channel. You can decide who from your organization is allowed to receive invitations to join another organization’s channel.

Manage who can notify a channel or workspace

By default, all members can notify a channel or workspace by using @channel, @here, and @everyone mentions. If they’d like, owners and admins can adjust these settings in their workspace or Enterprise organization.

Tip: On the Business+ and Enterprise plans, owners and admins can change who can use @here or @channel to notify members in any channel other than the general channel.

Require admin approval for invitations to Slack

By default, members (but not guests) can invite new members to your workspace. If you’d like, you can change this so that invitations must be requested and approved.

Note: When an invitation request is approved or denied, the member who requested it will be notified.

Manage invitation permissions

Use the steps below to manage whether workspace invitations must be approved.

  1. From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar.
  2. Select Workspace settings from the menu.
  3. Click the Permissions tab.
  4. Next to Invitations, click Expand.
  5. Check or uncheck the box next to Require admin approval.
  6. Click Save.

Note: Only owners and admins can manage guest accounts, and they will always need to approve members’ requests to invite guests.

Manage where invitation requests are sent

When admin approval is required, you can choose where invitation requests are sent — to all admins via Slack notification or to a specific channel.

  1. From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar.
  2. Select Workspace settings from the menu.
  3. Click the Permissions tab.
  4. Next to Invitations, click Expand and make sure the box next to Require admin approval is checked.
  5. Choose whether requests will be sent to all admins or routed to a channel.
  6. Click Save.

Manage invitation requests with APIs on Enterprise plans

Using a set of APIs, Org Owners and Org Admins can build a custom app for Slack to manage invitation requests for workspaces in their Enterprise organization. Apps built with these APIs can be connected to third-party services, like an identity provider (IDP) or IT ticketing software, to ensure new members are properly provisioned.

For more details and documentation, visit Slack API.

Note: When a custom invitation request management app is installed to an org, invitation requests will be sent to Org Owners and Admins. Workspace Owners and Admins will no longer receive invitation requests.

Who can use this feature?

  • Workspace Owners and** Workspace Admins**
  • Available on all plans

Set default channels for new members

To help onboard new members of your workspace, you can set default channels for them to automatically join. Default channels might include those related to company culture, policies, benefits, or anything else new members may need access to.

What to expect

  • You can only set public channels as default channels.
  • Members are automatically added to the #general channel and this can’t be changed.
  • Guests won’t be automatically added to default channels.

Note: Existing workspace members won’t be automatically added to default channels when you set them.

Add default channels

Free, Pro, and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

Workspace Owners and Admins can set default channels for their workspace.

  1. From your desktop, click ** Admin** in the sidebar.
  2. Select Workspace settings from the menu.
  3. Next to Default Channels, click Expand.
  4. Add channels you’d like new members to be added to by default.
  5. Click Save.
Org level

Org Owners and Admins can manage default channels for their org. To be set as a default channel, it must be public and an org-wide multi-workspace channel. An organization can have up to 25 default channels, and they can be set as optional or required.

To add default channels, use the steps below:

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Organization settings.
  3. Under Settings in the left column, click Channel Management.
  4. Under Default org-wide Channels, click Add a channel.
  5. Select a channel, then click Next.
  6. Choose if you’d like membership to be Optional or Required.
  7. Decide who can post in the channel. Then choose whether members can add threaded replies to messages posted in this channel.
  8. Click Next to review your changes.
  9. Click Save to finish.

Note: When you create a new default org-wide channel, all members of your org will be added to the channel.

Workspace level

Workspace Owners and Admins can set default channels for their workspace(s).

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click** Workspace settings**.
  3. Next to Default Channels, click Expand.
  4. Add channels you’d like new members to join by default.
  5. Click Save to finish.

Tip: Default channels can be customized when sending invitations to your workspace. Read more about inviting new members for details.

Remove default channels

Free, Pro, and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

Workspace Owners and Admins can remove default channels from their workspace.

  1. From your desktop, click your workspace name in the sidebar.
  2. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click** Workspace settings**.
  3. Next to Default Channels, click Expand.
  4. Click the small white x to the right of a channel name to remove it.
  5. Click Save to finish.
Org level

Org Owners and Admins can edit or remove default channels for their org.

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Organization settings.
  3. Under Settings in the left column, click Channel Management.
  4. Under Default org-wide channels, hover over a channel, then click the three dots icon to the right.
  5. Click Edit channel settings and make the adjustments you’d like.
  6. Click Next to review your changes.
  7. Click Save to finish.
Workspace level

Workspace Owners and Admins can remove default channels from their workspace(s).

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click** Workspace settings**.
  3. Next to Default Channels, click Expand.
  4. Click the small white x to the right of a channel name to remove it.
  5. Click Save to finish.

Who can use this feature?

  • Workspace Owners/Admins and Org Owners/Admins
  • Available on all plans

Set default Do Not Disturb hours

When default Do Not Disturb (DND) hours are set for a workspace or Enterprise organization, Slack will not send any desktop or mobile notifications to members during those hours. Setting default DND hours will affect all members of a workspace or org unless they set up their own DND schedule.

Add default Do Not Disturb hours

Free, Pro, and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

Here’s how Workspace Owners and Admins can set default DND hours:

  1. From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar.
  2. Select Workspace settings from the menu, then click Settings.
  3. Click Expand next to Do Not Disturb.
  4. Select the default hours when members will not receive notifications.
  5. Click Save.
Org level

Org Owners and Org Admins can add an org policy to set default DND hours for all workspaces in an org:

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Hover over Tools & settings, then click Organization settings.
  3. Click Settings in the left column. Then, click Organization Policies.
  4. Next to When to pause notifications, click Add Policy.
  5. Check the box next to Disable notifications during specific hours and select the default hours when members will not receive notifications.
  6. Click Save Policy.
Workspace level

Here’s how Workspace Owners and Workspace Admins can set default DND hours:

  1. Click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Hover over Tools & settings, then click Workspace settings from the menu. If you manage more than one workspace, choose one from the drop-down.
  3. Scroll down to Do Not Disturb and click Expand.
  4. Select the default hours when members will not receive notifications.
  5. Click Save.

Note: When you set default Do Not Disturb hours, members will still be able to change their own hours, set a DND schedule, or turn DND off.

Who can use this feature?

  • Workspace Owners/Admins and Org Owners/Admins
  • Available on all plans

Set the default language of a workspace or organization

Select the default language for members of your Slack workspace or Enterprise organization. Email invitations and SCIM-synced profiles will display in the default language, but everything else in Slack will be determined by members’ individual language preferences.

Free, Pro, and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

Org Owners and Org Admins can set the default language for workspaces in their Enterprise organization using the steps below. The default language will apply to any new members or workspaces added to the organization, but it won’t override members’ changes to their individual language preferences.

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.

Set up and manage Salesforce channels in Slack

Salesforce channels allow your team to update Salesforce records and centralize conversations about customers right in Slack. You can create and manage channel configurations to control which record types can be used in Salesforce channels.

Note: You can also set up Salesforce channels to let members collaborate directly on Salesforce records. Visit the Salesforce Help Center to learn more.

Configure Salesforce channels

Follow the steps below to set up Salesforce channels in Slack. Work with an Admin in Salesforce to complete the setup steps in Salesforce.

Step 1: Connect a Salesforce org to Slack
  1. Follow the steps in our Connect Salesforce and Slack guide.
  2. Once your Salesforce org is connected, you’ll need to manually map users if they haven’t already been granted access to Salesforce in Slack.
Step 2: Create Salesforce channel configurations

Create a configuration for each record type your members can use when they create a Salesforce channel. Salesforce channels can map to any record type except Users.

  1. Sign in to Salesforce, then select Setup.
  2. In the Quick Find box, search for and select Slack Channels for Records.
  3. Click + Add Objects.
  4. Search for and select the objects that you want to use for Salesforce channels.
  5. Click Add Objects to finish.

Note: The default privacy setting for a Salesforce channel configuration is based on the object type’s record access settings in Salesforce. If the object is set to public in Salesforce, the default will be Public. For all other settings, the default will be Limited access.

Manage Salesforce channel default settings

For each Salesforce record type, you can choose defaults for the following settings:

  • Channel names
  • Channel privacy
  • List tabs

Salesforce channel names will match the names of their corresponding records, but you can choose to map them to other fields in Salesforce. Here’s how to adjust default settings for Salesforce channels:

Free, Pro, and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

  1. From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar.

  2. Select Manage Salesforce Organizations from the menu.

  3. Select a Salesforce org.

  4. Click the Channel configurations tab.

  5. Click the three dots icon next to a Salesforce channel configuration, then click Edit default preferences.

  6. Adjust your settings, then click Save.

  7. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.

  8. Hover over Tools & settings, then click Manage Salesforce Organizations.

  9. Select a Salesforce org.

  10. Click the Channel configurations tab.

  11. Click the three dots icon next to a Salesforce channel configuration, then click Edit default preferences.

  12. Adjust your settings, then click Save.

Note: If you use the record name field as your default channel name, the channel name will automatically update in Slack when the record name changes in Salesforce.

Manage default privacy settings

When you configure default privacy settings for Salesforce channels, you can decide whether channels are public or limited access. If you limit access to a Salesforce channel, you can further customize who can view and join based on the following Salesforce record permissions:

  • Anyone who can view record Anyone with access to the Salesforce record can view the channel and invite others.
  • Record editors People who can edit the Salesforce record can view the channel and invite others.
  • Record owners Only record owners and those with transfer access can view the channel and invite others.

Free, Pro, and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

  1. From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar.

  2. Select Manage Salesforce Organizations from the menu.

  3. Select a Salesforce org.

  4. Click the Channel configurations tab.

  5. Click the three dots icon next to a Salesforce channel configuration, then click Edit default preferences.

  6. Below Channel privacy,select a default privacy. If you select Limited access, choose a Salesforce record permission level from the drop-down menu.

  7. Choose Save to finish.

  8. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.

  9. Hover over Tools & settings, then click Manage Salesforce Organizations.

  10. Select a Salesforce org.

  11. Click the Channel configurations tab.

  12. Click the three dots icon next to a Salesforce channel configuration, then click Edit default preferences.

  13. Below Channel privacy,select a default privacy. If you select Limited access, choose a Salesforce record permission level from the drop-down menu.

  14. Choose Save to finish.

Note: For more on how privacy for Salesforce channels differs from regular channels, visit Security for Salesforce channels.

Manage Salesforce record previews

When someone shares a Salesforce record in a channel or direct message (DM), a preview will appear containing record details. You can restrict the details that appear in record previews and allow exceptions for certain record object types (like Account or Opportunity) to override these restrictions. Here are the options:

  • Show record details (default) Record name, object, and record details (such as Stage or Amount) are shown.
  • Show name and object only No additional fields are shown
  • Show object only Only the record object type is shown

Note: Record previews are visible to all members of the conversation they appear in, regardless of member permissions in Salesforce. Visit Security for Salesforce channels to learn more about permissions for record previews.

Slack data loss prevention

With data loss prevention (DLP) for Slack, you can reduce the risk of sharing confidential, malicious, or personally identifiable information in your Slack organization. Slack DLP scans messages, text-based files, and canvases sent by members of your organization for content that violates rules you create.

image (2).png

How it works

  • Org Primary Owners and members with the Roles Admin system role can assign the DLP Admin system role to members.
  • DLP Admins can create customized rules using PCRE (PHP) regex syntax, or choose from several preconfigured rules to scan for messages and files in Slack that may require administrative action.
  • Rules can be further customized to apply only in specific conversation types and workspaces in your Enterprise organization.
  • DLP Admins will receive a daily summary of rule violations and can take action on messages and files from the DLP dashboard.

Note: While DLP scans most content in Slack, certain types of data aren’t scanned at this time.

Create DLP rules

You can write your own custom rules or choose from several preconfigured rules to scan Slack for data like credit card numbers, API tokens, or personally identifiable information. When creating a rule, DLP Admins can choose to take one of the following actions when a rule is violated:

  • Display DLP dashboard alert only

  • Show a warning to members who violate a DLP rule*

  • Hide (or “tombstone”) messages or files until they can be reviewed

  • Member warnings can’t be displayed on canvases or snippets that violate a DLP rule.

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Hover over Tools & settings from the menu, then click Organization settings.
  3. Click Security in the left sidebar, then choose Data loss prevention.
  4. Click Create Rule in the top-right corner.
  5. Under Rule name, choose a name for your rule.
  6. Select an option from the drop-down menu to choose a preconfigured rule or click Use custom regular expression and enter a regex string you’d like to track.
  7. Select an Action to take and (if applicable) customize the text that appears when your rule is violated, then click Next.
  8. Choose whether your rule applies to Slack Connect conversations, specific workspaces, and specific conversation types in your grid org.
  9. Click Save Rule to finish.
Types of preconfigured rules

Slack DLP comes with a library of built-in detection rules organized into three categories:

  • Credit card numbers Credit card rules match each major network’s published number format and validate every match to confirm it’s a real card number
  • National identifiers National identifier rules cover several common government-issued IDs. Where an identifier includes a check digit, the rule validates it as an added filter.
  • Secrets (APIs and tokens) Secret and API key rules match the format of major cloud and SaaS providers like AWS, GitHub, Stripe, and more.

Note: Preconfigured DLP rules have been developed by Slack using algorithms based on industry best practices. Please note that preconfigured rules may not detect all targeted data and conversely, they may detect false positives.

Manage DLP rules

You can edit a DLP rule to change it, or deactivate a rule you no longer need.

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Hover over Tools & settings from the menu, then click Organization settings.
  3. Click Security in the left sidebar, then choose Data loss prevention.
  4. Under the Rules tab, click the three dots icon next to the rule you’d like to change.
  5. Choose Edit or Deactivate and follow the prompts.
  6. Click Save Rule or Deactivate to finish.

Manage DLP rule violations

When a member of your organization sends a message that violates a DLP rule, you’ll see an alert in the Slack DLP dashboard. From the dashboard, you can then archive the alert, delete the message, or restore the message (if it was hidden). Remember that alerts expire after 90 days and will be removed from the DLP dashboard.

  1. From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar.
  2. Hover over Tools & settings from the menu, then click Organization settings.
  3. Click Security in the left sidebar, then choose Data loss prevention.
  4. Under the Alerts tab, click a flagged message, then select an action. To manage violations in bulk, check the box next to as many flagged messages as you like, then select an action at top of the table.

Note: People are notified if their flagged messages or files are deleted.

Unsupported content types

The following content types are not scanned by DLP:

  • Non-text files such as images, videos, or audio files
  • AI summaries
  • Canvases in Slack Connect conversations
  • Channel names
  • File names
  • Files uploaded via a channel tab but not shared elsewhere in Slack
  • Profile data
  • Search results
  • Slack lists
  • Workflow data that isn’t sent as a message in Slack (ex., text that appears in a form)
  • Any files over 100 MB in size
  • Files hosted externally (such as in a third-party file sharing app)

Who can use this feature?

  • Members with the DLP Admin system role
  • Available on Enterprise plans

Transfer ownership of a workspace or org

Organizations change, so that might mean primary ownership of a Slack workspace or org may need to change too. We’ve outlined how to transfer primary ownership, so keep reading to learn more.

I’m the Primary Owner

If you’re the Primary Owner of a workspace or Enterprise org, you can transfer ownership to another member.

What to expect
  • You’ll need to enter your password to confirm the transfer.
  • The transfer will happen immediately.
  • Your role will change from Primary Owner to Owner.
  • Need to deactivate your account? You’ll need to transfer primary ownership first.
Transfer ownership

Free, Pro, and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

  1. Visit the transfer ownership page.
  2. Search for and select the member you’d like to be the new Workspace Primary Owner.
  3. Enter your password to confirm the transfer.
  4. Click the Transfer Workspace Ownership button to finish.

There are two types of primary ownership within an Enterprise org — a single Org Primary Owner, and multiple Workspace Primary Owners.

Transfer ownership of a workspace

In an Enterprise org, Workspace Primary Owners can transfer ownership of their workspace to another member.

  1. Visit the transfer ownership page.
  2. Search for and select the member you’d like to be the new Workspace Primary Owner.
  3. Enter your password to confirm the transfer.
  4. Click the Transfer Workspace Ownership button to finish.
Transfer ownership of an org

The Primary Org Owner can choose to transfer primary ownership to another member. If you’re the Org Primary Owner, here’s how to contact us:

  1. Use this form to send us a note.
  2. Include the new Org Primary Owner’s email address.
  3. Our team will get in touch to help you complete the transfer.

Tip: Consider working with your new Primary Owner to ensure details like billing information remain accurate.

I’m not the Primary Owner

Free, Pro, and Business+ plans

Enterprise plans

Step 1: Contact the Primary Owner

Only a Primary Owner can transfer ownership. Try reaching out to the Primary Owner first to request that they transfer their role directly to someone else. If you’re not sure who the Primary Owner is, visit the About This Workspace page to confirm.

If the Primary Owner is no longer available (for example, if they’ve left your organization or can’t be reached), Slack may be able to help transfer the Primary Owner role. Review the steps below to see if your workspace qualifies and what information you’ll need to include when you contact us.

Note: Slack may be able to help transfer the Primary Owner role for workspaces owned by a company, institution, or other legal entity, but we can’t guarantee that every situation will qualify.

Step 2: Check if your workspace qualifies

Slack can only consider requests to transfer the Primary Owner role if both the following criteria are met:

  • The workspace was created on behalf of a legal entity, such as a company, organization, or educational institution
  • The request is submitted or authorized by a senior staff member who can represent that entity, such as a director-level employee or someone in an equivalent leadership position.

If these requirements aren’t met, Slack may not be able to transfer the Primary Owner role.

If the workspace was created by the Primary Owner on their own behalf (for example, to support a personal project, club, or community group) and not on behalf of a company or other legal entity, Slack cannot assist with a request to transfer the Primary Owner role.

Step 3: Gather what you’ll need

Before contacting Slack for assistance, make sure you have the following information ready.

  • The workspace URL (for example, yourworkspace.slack.com)
  • Primary Owner details: Who currently holds the role, their email address, and how that account is connected to your organization.
  • The proposed new Primary Owner: Include the name and email address of the person you’d like to transfer the Primary Owner role to. Make sure they’re already a member of your workspace, and their account uses an email address on your company’s domain — we can’t transfer ownership to personal email addresses.
Step 4: Submit your request

After you’ve tried internal options and confirmed your workspace qualifies, reach out to Slack Support. We’ll review the details, and follow up with next steps if we need more information from you.

Please keep in mind that transfers of the Primary Owner role go through a careful review process, may take time, and aren’t guaranteed to be approved.

If your Org Primary Owner has left the organization or can’t be reached, Slack can help transfer the org primary owner role to another member. Here’s how to contact us:

  1. Use this form to send us a note.
  2. Include the new Org Primary Owner’s email address.
  3. Our team will get in touch to help you complete the transfer.

Tip: You can always create your own workspace if needed — this would make you the Primary Owner of the new workspace.

Who can use this feature?

  • Only the Primary Owner can transfer ownership of a workspace or org
  • Available on all plans
